item.title: When is the next full moon for Ursaluna in Pokémon Go?
item.description: If you want Ursaluna in Pokémon Go , you'll need to evolve your Ursaring on specific evenings. Ursaring only evolves into its grizzly evolution, Ursaluna, when there's a full moon in real life ! Full moons occur once a month, so if the full moon passes, you'll need to wait another month or so to evolve it, sadly.

item.title: A Strange Quantum Theorem Has Killed Einstein’s Reality
item.description: One of a human’s earliest developmental milestones is an understanding of object permanence. It generally takes less than a year for a baby to realize that when an adult hides their face behind their hands in a game of peek-a-boo, they don’t cease to exist. There’s more to the world around us than what we perceive. This suggests — or at least, it suggested to Albert Einstein — that the world is… Source

item.title: Global stocks plunge amid AI slowdown fears after Democrats’ midterm triumph
item.description: Asian and European markets follow Wall Street with sharp fall as FTSE down 1.9% Business live – latest updates European stock markets have fallen sharply as a rout in US tech stocks spread across the Atlantic, after the Democrats’ midterms victory sparked fears of a slowdown in the AI industry. A sell-off on Wall Street on Thursday was followed by sharp falls in Asian stocks markets on Friday. The investor sentiment then reached London, where the market was, at one stage, poised for its worst day since March. Continue reading...

item.title: Global Lacrosse Games roster breakdown: Canada women
item.description: Canada is consistently one of the top two nations in the world in women’s lacrosse, and has been for decades. This country has produced some of the greatest lacrosse players in history, like the legendary Dana Dobbie. We are bound to see more greatness from this squad that has a No. 1 ranking in mind to chase after. The roster Canada has put together for the Lexus Global Lacrosse Games is an exciting mixture of seasoned leaders and exploding stars. Let’s break it down. Field Players Erica Evans Annabel Child Jordan Dean Milana Zizakovic Kassidy Morris Aurora Cordingley Maggie Cuddy Nicole Perroni Megan Kinna Madalyn Baxter Kylea Dobson Goalies Kameron Halsall Alecia Nicholas One word to describe this roster is… Poised. This Canadian team is primed and prepped for a big tournament. They have battled to the very end against USA the last few times the rival nations have matched up in a Sixes Championship, and are likely itching to get over that hump. Players like Erica Evans , Megan Kinna, Nicole Perroni and Aurora Cordingley have played on these big stages in a Canadian uniform before. Evans brings a decade of familiarity alone, playing with the Canadian national team since 2015. Their experience from playing for Canada for many years will bring a level of poise and comfort to the Global Lacrosse Games that’s needed to thrive and win against the other top nations in the world. Biggest star: Erica Evans Evans is coming off a championship summer with the Maryland Charm and has been an international star since she won a gold medal with the U19 Canadian team. She started off a historic run by being named to that 2015 All-World Team and has since been an All-World selection in nearly every international event she has participated in – in all disciplines: field, Sixes and box. She is a strong lefty and dominant force in the middle of the field, sparking transition plays and coming up with big caused turnovers. Her offensive IQ is next-level; she executes two-player games seamlessly and constantly opens up scoring opportunities for herself and others. Evans will be the main all-around Canadian player to keep an eye on throughout each game. Breakout candidate: Kameron Halsall Halsall is the type of goalkeeper who can make or break the outcome of a game. She stands tall in the crease and is a strong-handed lefty who clears the ball quickly the moment she makes a save in order to provide scoring opportunities for her offense going the other way. She is one of the goalies who thrives in a Sixes setting due to substantial breakaway shot opportunities that result from the fast pace of games. Halsall’s patience to not bite on shooters’ fakes and her ability to make a last-second sprawling stop are two of her many game-altering abilities as Canada’s main keeper. item.content:encoded: Canada is consistently one of the top two nations in the world in women’s lacrosse, and has been for decades. This country has produced some of the greatest lacrosse players in history, like the legendary Dana Dobbie. We are bound to see more greatness from this squad that has a No. 1 ranking in mind to chase after. The roster Canada has put together for the Lexus Global Lacrosse Games is an exciting mixture of seasoned leaders and exploding stars. Let’s break it down. Field Players Erica Evans Annabel Child Jordan Dean Milana Zizakovic Kassidy Morris Aurora Cordingley Maggie Cuddy Nicole Perroni Megan Kinna Madalyn Baxter Kylea Dobson Goalies Kameron Halsall Alecia Nicholas One word to describe this roster is… Poised. This Canadian team is primed and prepped for a big tournament. They have battled to the very end against USA the last few times the rival nations have matched up in a Sixes Championship, and are likely itching to get over that hump. Players like Erica Evans , Megan Kinna, Nicole Perroni and Aurora Cordingley have played on these big stages in a Canadian uniform before. Evans brings a decade of familiarity alone, playing with the Canadian national team since 2015. Their experience from playing for Canada for many years will bring a level of poise and comfort to the Global Lacrosse Games that’s needed to thrive and win against the other top nations in the world. Biggest star: Erica Evans Evans is coming off a championship summer with the Maryland Charm and has been an international star since she won a gold medal with the U19 Canadian team. She started off a historic run by being named to that 2015 All-World Team and has since been an All-World selection in nearly every international event she has participated in – in all disciplines: field, Sixes and box. She is a strong lefty and dominant force in the middle of the field, sparking transition plays and coming up with big caused turnovers. Her offensive IQ is next-level; she executes two-player games seamlessly and constantly opens up scoring opportunities for herself and others. Evans will be the main all-around Canadian player to keep an eye on throughout each game. Breakout candidate: Kameron Halsall Halsall is the type of goalkeeper who can make or break the outcome of a game. She stands tall in the crease and is a strong-handed lefty who clears the ball quickly the moment she makes a save in order to provide scoring opportunities for her offense going the other way. She is one of the goalies who thrives in a Sixes setting due to substantial breakaway shot opportunities that result from the fast pace of games. Halsall’s patience to not bite on shooters’ fakes and her ability to make a last-second sprawling stop are two of her many game-altering abilities as Canada’s main keeper. They can win it all if… They avoid the penalty box. In one of Canada’s most recent matchups against USA in the Pan-American Sixes Championship in October, penalties stacked up toward the end of the game and allowed the Americans the chance to win. More penalties means more precious time spent with one less player on the field, which is a situation all teams try to avoid whenever possible. This is especially true in Sixes, where the momentum can swing even faster than in the full-field game because multiple goals can be scored in a matter of seconds without wasting any penalty time resetting at the draw. Learning from these errors and working hard to avoid penalties, especially late in tight games, will be imminent to Canada’s success in the Global Lacrosse Games. Biggest concern: Depth Star power is no issue for Canada. From Evans to Halsall, Cordingley to Dean, Kinna to Perroni, this Canadian roster is stacked. The true question is whether their depth will be able to match up to that of the United States roster. Every time these two countries play against one another, it’s a highly anticipated contest. Rivalry games like these often come down to the wire, and the unsung heroes coming from the depths of the roster typically end up being the game-changers. This time around will be an excellent test for Canada’s depth and an all-time game for us lacrosse fans to tune into. Stat to know: 1 goal The last time Canada won a women’s gold medal was at the 2022 World Games, when it beat USA by a close score of 14-12. Since then, the USA has consistently been triumphant in international matchups, though Canada has kept the score close, staying within a one-goal margin multiple times. The final score of the 2023 World Lacrosse Super Sixes event was 8-7 in favor of the Americans, and the Canadians most recently lost a 15-14 thriller at the 2026 Pan-American Sixes Lacrosse Championship. Can this roster break the one-goal curse when it lines up against the USA on Dec. 11? Having a taste of gold from 2022 and bringing that motivation into every international matchup definitely fuels the fire behind this Canadian team. We’ll get a chance to witness Canada’s spark in action starting on Dec. 9 against the Haudenosaunee at 5:30 p.m. ET. Explore here for more information on the Lexus Global Lacrosse Games.

item.title: Premier League legends at odds over 'overrated' Bradley Barcola following $167 million move
item.description: Bradley Barcola joined Liverpool in the summer from Paris Saint-Germain -Credit:Carl Recine, Getty Images Glen Johnson has addressed comments from France FIFA World Cup winner Emmanuel Petit, suggesting Liverpool overpaid for 'overrated' £123 million ($166.6 million) summer acquisition Bradley Barcola. The former Reds defender has expressed confidence that the winger will find his form following a challenging beginning to his Anfield tenure. Barcola toiled in an unaccustomed striker's position on Wednesday as Liverpool's flawless UEFA Champions League league phase record ended with a 3-2 loss to Fenerbahçe in Istanbul. The France international had shone in his prior Champions League road fixture, delivering an impressive hat-trick during the 6-3 winat LASK. -Credit:Laurence Griffiths, Getty Images However, those strikes represent the sole goals Barcola has managed across his 13 outings for the Reds following his blockbuster transfer from European champions Paris Saint-Germain on August 31. Earlier this month, former Arsenal, Barcelona, and Chelsea midfielder Petit, who captured the World Cup with France in 1998, stated via the Liverpool Echo : "£120m? I would never put that price tag on the table. We all know that in France. "We know that he is a quality player, he could sometimes be great, but he doesn't have consistency during games. He was good most of the time with Paris because of the whole team behind him. I would probably have spent £60m or £70m, maximum. That's my opinion. It's becoming common now that English clubs are spending so much money on overrated players." However, Johnson, who registered 200 appearances for Liverpool with nine goals and 13 assists following his £17.5 million (around $29 million) transfer from Portsmouth in June 2009, considers Barcola "world-class" and argues he shouldn't be evaluated solely on his price tag. He said: "I don't think Barcola is overrated. I think he's world-class. I've been a fan of his for a long time. I think he's brilliant. To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE "I think what Manu Petit is trying to say is that he wasn't worth that money. I think that's what he meant. There's no doubt about his talent, his ability and obviously fans have the right to think whether he's world class or not. That's up to them. "But I think what Manu was actually meaning was the fact that there's some other players who are really good that are going for half the money. "So I think he meant more of that, than actually being not as good as people say. Because that's two different things. You need the talent there to compete with each other. I was hoping Liverpool would sign him before. The financial stuff, that has nothing to do with us. We just want to see the best players at Liverpool and how they can get it done. To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE "I think what Manu Petit is trying to say is that he wasn't worth that money. I think that's what he meant. I was hoping Liverpool would sign him before. The financial stuff, that has nothing to do with us. We just want to see the best players at Liverpool and how they can get it done. "And the best players will play. And the ones that aren't playing have to improve. It can only be a good level of competition." With Barcola's French international teammate Hugo Ekitike still on the sidelines, Reds manager Andoni Iraola nevertheless boasts an abundance of attacking talent to call upon. • Chelsea's Cole Palmer snubbed by Thomas Tuchel as latest England squad announced • Avram Glazer breaks silence on Manchester United's commercial power amid fan protests Cody Gakpo, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Muñoz, alongside Barcola, are all vying for the two wide positions, while Lewis Koumas has impressed the new head coach sufficiently to emerge as a credible backup to Alexander Isak up front as Ekitike continues his rehabilitation from a serious injury. Isak notched his seventh goal in 13 appearances when he headed Liverpool ahead against Fenerbahçe, and after a difficult debut season with the 20-time English champions hampered by fitness concerns, the £125 million recruit from Newcastle United is beginning to hit his stride "No one wants to be injured, but I think it's very important for attacking players to have games under your belt," said Johnson, speaking to PariuriX.com . "A rhythm of games to find that flair and the confidence to pull the things off that they can do so well. "So it's hard for them if they're in one game, out for two, back for two, out for one. It's very hard to get that consistency. But his ability is not questionable. It might be hard to rely on him in terms of when he's available." Liverpool round out their schedule before the international break on Sunday with a trip to struggling Crystal Palace in the Premier League.

item.title: Where to watch Grand Slam of Curling Masters: Schedule, times, channels, live streams, scores for 2026
item.description: Where to watch Grand Slam of Curling Masters: Schedule, times, channels, live streams, scores for 2026 originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The 2026 Grand Slam of Curling series continues this week with the GSOC Masters from Alberta. Based on the opener three weeks ago in Victoria, the teams to beat in Medicine Hat will be Team Schwaller on the men's side and Team Einarson on the women's. It was the second GSOC win for Yannick Schwaller and the seventh for Canadian stalwart Kerri Einarson. Everyone will be gunning for those two teams, but there are plenty of other contenders including two other Canadian favourites in defending champions Team Dunstone in the men's division and Team Homan on the women's side. Here's all you need to know to watch all the action this week. Where to watch Grand Slam of Curling Masters TV channels: CBC, Sportsnet Live streams: Fubo , Sportsnet+, Rock Channel Fans can stream the entire Grand Slam of Curling Masters via Rock Channel, which will have exclusive live coverage of the morning draws each day, along with games not selected for featured spots on the main broadcast the rest of the day. One featured game during the afternoon and evening draws will air on Sportsnet channels and Sportsnet+ from Tuesday through Friday, along with Saturday's quarterfinals and Sunday's finals. The men's and women's semifinals will air on CBC and Sportsnet+ and can also be streamed via Fubo . Grand Slam of Curling Masters schedule, scores 2026 All times listed below are Eastern. item.title: VfB Stuttgart vs. Werder Bremen preview: Undav and Füllkrug in contrasting form ahead of Topspiel
item.description: VfB Stuttgart vs. Werder Bremen preview: Undav and Füllkrug in contrasting form ahead of Topspiel Deniz Undav's VfB Stuttgart will host Niclas Füllkrug's Werder Bremen in the marquee fixture of matchday 10. VfB Stuttgart The captain's goal drought contributed to Stuttgart's slow start to the season. Undav had found the net twice, but none of those goals came in the league as his poor form led him to miss out on Jürgen Klopp's squad nomination for the second time. Meanwhile, Ermedin Demirović has been their go-to guy this season, although he was unable to score in the defeat against Galatasaray, who had an unsuccessful attempt to sign the Bosnian striker in the summer. Stuttgart returned to winning ways in Bundesliga on matchday 8 after successive defeats. Team News The absence of Atakan Karazor and Angelo Stiller in midfield would cause selection issues for Hoeneß, although the former has a slight chance to recover from an injury that forced his early substitution against Galatasaray. Demirović and Undav started together against both Leverkusen and the Turkish champions, although Hoeneß preferred different playing systems. In goal, Dennis Seimen is expected to return in place of the experienced Fabian Bredlow. Werder Bremen After matching Rudi Völler's club record of scoring in seven successive Bundesliga games, Füllkrug earned a national team call-up by Klopp on Thursday. The 33-year-old leads the scoring chart in Bundesliga, and he already opened a five-goal lead over a certain Harry Kane. The nine goals from the former Torjägerkanone winner helped Werder Bremen to start the matchday in fifth place after having to fight relegation consistently in past seasons. Daniel Thioune’s troops are unbeaten in Bundesliga since starting the campaign with a 4-1 defeat to Freiburg. Team News Mitchell Weiser suffered another injury setback inside the first 15 minutes in last week's 2-0 win over TSG Hoffenheim, and he'll miss this one at the very least. Eren Dinkci, who scored the second goal after replacing him, is expected to start in the right wing. Head-to-head Werder Bremen are unbeaten in their last two trips to Stuttgart, although the Swabians did win 4-0 at Weserstadion last season. The last time a game between the two sides ended goalless was in February 2006. Predicted Lineups Click here to see our predicted Stuttgart vs. Werder Bremen lineups.

The last Section 2 team to repeat at states was Waterford-Halfmoon, which won the Class C title in 2022 and shared it with Mount Academy in 2023. 6. The Bethlehem boys' soccer team is the only Section 2 team still undefeated and competing. The Eagles (15-0-3) are one of 10 undefeated boys' teams across all classes in the NYSPHAA field. Their opponent on Saturday is Watertown, which is also undefeated at 19-0-0. Averill Park junior Teagan DeLair and Gianna Lovell celebrate a goal during the Section 2 Class A finals against Schalmont on Tuesday. (Jim Franco/Times Union) 7. Four Section 2 schools sent teams to the state playoffs for both boys' and girls' soccer: Bethlehem (Class AA), Averill Park (Class A), Schuylerville (Class B) and Northville (Class D). Seven of those teams play Saturday, while Northville girls' soccer was eliminated in a sub-regional game earlier this week. 8. Sami Terra scored a hat trick to lift the Shaker boys' soccer team to a 3-1 win over Class AAA defending co-champion Guilderland in the sectional final. The senior has returned from an injury to score 17 goals this season for the Blue Bison. 9. Bethlehem girls' soccer is back in the state tournament for the first time since 2019. That season, the Eagles reached the state quarterfinals with current U.S. women's national team player Claire Hutton playing a starring role as an eighth grader. 10. The Averill Park boys' soccer team (8-9-2) has lost only once in its past seven games, a 2-1 setback to Class AAA champion Shaker. The Golden Knights finished 2-9-1 in Suburban Council play, but defeated Hudson Falls, Cohoes and Schalmont in the playoffs, outscoring them 15-3 to claim their first sectional title since 2021. Northville's Magnus Halloran celebrates his goal against Hartford in the Section 2 Class D championship game at Queensbury High School in Queensbury, NY on Saturday, October 31, 2026. (Stephen Weaver) 11. The Northville boys' soccer team defeated Hartford 5-0 to claim its third consecutive Class D title. The Falcons (18-1) have won eight straight games, outscoring opponents 59-0 over that span and allowing only five goals all season. Northville's lone loss this season came against the No. 1 Class D team in the state, Chazy, in early October. 12. It's been an immediate success for Bethlehem girls' soccer coach Scott Geis. He has the Eagles in the state playoffs in his first year as varsity coach. 13. Two first-year Section 2 boys' soccer coaches have led their teams to the state regionals. Greenville's boys' soccer team is led by head coach Jared McAneny, the uncle of Spartans' star Isaac McAneny. The Averill Park boys' soccer team is led by coach Dylan Martin. 14. The Black Horses are on the rise. Schuylerville girls' soccer had never reached a Section 2 final before last year. Now, they've been to two championship games in a row, and this year they unseated defending champion Mechanicville to get into the state tournament. 15. How about this high-powered rematch in Class AAA? Shenendehowa girls' soccer is the No. 1 team in the latest state rankings. The Mustangs face the No. 2 team, Section 3's Cicero-North Syracuse, in Saturday's regional final. The two teams met in early October, with Shen winning 3-0. Isaac McAneny after scoring the winning goal against Maple Hill in overtime of the Section 2 Class C championship game at Queensbury High School. (Stephen Weaver) 16. The Greenville boys' soccer team (16-3-1) won the Section 2 Class B title last season by defeating Mechanicville, then moved to Class C before this season began. At 6-0-1, the No. 2-ranked Spartans are unbeaten against Class C teams this season. Greenville beat defending champion Maple Hill 1-0 in overtime on a goal by Isaac McAneny and earned a sub-regional win over the state's sixth-ranked team, Burke Catholic, from Section 9. 17. Brittany Tetlack is powering a dangerous attack for Shenendehowa girls' soccer . The junior striker scored a hat trick in the Mustangs' sectional final win over Guilderland and has 24 goals this season. 18. Northville boys' soccer goalkeeper Joey Capobianco earned his 16th shutout of the season in the Falcons' 5-0 Section 2 Class D final over Hartford, breaking the Northville school record for most shutouts in a season. Stillwater's Kamryn VanPelt navigates through Lake George defenders during the Section 2 Class C championship game last Saturday at Lansingburgh High School. (Kyle Adams/For the Times Union) 19. Stillwater girls' soccer is on a roll. Since losing to Mechanicville in late September, the defending Class C state champions have won 13 consecutive games and outscored its opposition 67-3. 20. After losing to Broadalbin-Perth 1-0 in last year's sectional tournament, the Schuylerville boys' soccer team (13-3-2) beat the Patriots 1-0 in this year's Class B final, with Colden Harrison's golden goal in overtime. The win marked Schuylerville's first sectional title since 2019. 21. Teagan DeLair has been at the center of the late-season surge for Averill Park girls' soccer . item.title: Forget the schedule, Jalen Brunson has another theory to explain the NBA injury crisis
item.description: Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images Almost every team in the NBA has been hit by injuries this season. We are less than a month into the new campaign, and several big names have already been sidelined due to one issue or another. There are fears that the list could grow in the coming weeks and months. Many feel the schedule is the reason why, but Jalen Brunson has a different theory. Jalen Brunson says the NBA’s injury crisis could be down to ‘style of play’ It has been a real shame to see several fantastic players miss games due to injuries this season. From Anthony Edwards and Ja Morant to Paolo Banchero and Kawhi Leonard, many are currently sidelined, causing their respective teams to be significantly weaker. Several theories have been going around – from the gruelling schedule to a lack of preparation in pre-season practice sessions. But Jalen Brunson thinks it may actually be down to the style of play most coaches employ in the NBA in today’s game. When told that 16-20 per cent of the league is on the injury report, Brunson said on the Roommates Show : “I just feel like it’s a lot. “Is the schedule asking too much of the players? No! I mean, the schedule is the schedule. It’s been that way for – we’ve been playing 82 games for, I don’t know how many years – like decades. “But it’s obviously unfortunate things happen, but yeah, I don’t think it’s the scheduling part. I think maybe it’s like the style of play. We’re playing fast-paced basketball.” The intensity involved in almost every team sport in the world has gone up in recent years, and it is showing no signs of slowing down. That has definitely made games more interesting, but it has to be said that the physical burden on players has gone up as well. That increases the risk of injuries, which we are all seeing right now. item.title: Central Falls, Classical head to the D-II boys soccer championship
item.description: JOHNSTON — Central Falls might have that magic. And Classical survived on grit. The Warriors were relentless for 80 minutes against Mt. Hope to continue their unexpected playoff run. A pair of goals from Daniel Rios Aceituno paced a 3-1 comeback in a Division II semifinal victory over the Huskies. Peter Breen closed out an unending night between Classical vs. Central in the second semifinal. The senior’s penalty kick lifted the Purple to a 0-0 (6-5) victory after eight penalty rounds on a breezy, Nov. 5 night at Johnston High School. Watch RI high school games on NFHS Network The eighth-ranked Huskies and third-ranked Purple advance to the championship at Rhode Island College on Sunday at 2:30 p.m. It’s the first title appearance for Central Falls, who are looking for their fifth championship overall, since it won a D-III crown in 2005. Classical advances to a title round for the first time since 2014 when it won a D-II championship. Central Falls won the season meeting against Classical, 4-1, in Providence in mid-September. “I told the team to keep our head up,” Rios Aceituno said. “Just keep it up and keep pushing. We've been working hard in practice every day.” “Right before I take that kick, I know what I'm going to do,” Breen said. “I feel calm. If the goalie guesses right, he guesses. But if he doesn't, that's awesome and we’re in the championship on Sunday.” Read on below for more on the D-II boys soccer semifinals. Central Falls strikes late The Warriors dominated possession in the first half against No. 4 Mt. Hope but trailed at halftime after a clinical set-piece header from Gavin Avila in the 17th minute. After turning back No. 1 Smithfield in penalty kicks in the quarterfinals, the upset kings still had plenty of fuel for the final 40 minutes. Kevin Ramos Pedroza provided the first cross that Rios Aceituno cleaned up with a header to the left corner with 27 minutes left. Second-chance opportunities were the Warriors’ best scoring looks against Mt. Hope keeper Cole Tavares. The senior stood on his head, but Central Falls broke through and was onto the championship from there. “We just told [each other] that we have to stay calm,” Oscar Veliz Catalan said. “It doesn't matter what the scoreboard is, we just have to keep our head up. It doesn't matter if it's 2-0. Just keep our head up.” Rios Aceituno provided the helper on the second goal with a tough angle to the short post before Veliz Catalan buried for the go-ahead goal with 8:03 left. Rios Aceituno added the insurance with five minutes left. “We came from last season, we came from not winning a game [in D-I],” Veliz Catalan said. “We came [into the year] with a good mindset, and I feel like this year really means a lot.” Classical wins in shootout Goalie Senai Zerit knew penalty kicks were coming early into the second half and everyone at Johnston knew they were in for a long night. It doesn't matter if it's 2-0. The stadium lights were on a timer to shut off at 10 p.m. and that deadline was even pushed back twice. Zerit and Breen made sure a third extension wasn’t needed. Zerit made his second save of the shootout before Breen delivered the winner. Celebration ensued at the 15-yard line as Classical denied Central a third straight penalty-shootout win in these playoffs. “It's just a lot of emotions,” Zerit said. “At the beginning of the penalty shootout, I'm just trying to stay calm and just stay confident and not let the doubt come into my mind. “I knew when there was 30 minutes left in the second half [penalty kicks were coming]. We weren't really breaking through, it was really a stalemate because Central wasn't really attacking a lot. They were kind of sitting back and defending because they've already won two shootouts in the past. I think they were really pushing for the shootout, thinking they could take it.” Both teams moved down to the state’s second league this year after finishing at the bottom of the D-I table. The Purple finished this season with their first winning record since 2019. “This feels pretty great,” Breen said. “We have not had a winning record in a long time. … We've lost a lot in the last years, so it just feels crazy.” This article originally appeared on The Providence Journal: Central Falls, Classical head to the D-II boys soccer championship Our editors independently choose our recommendations. item.title: Worcestershire trio aim to make more Cup magic
item.description: It's now 55 seasons since non-league Hereford United's 2-1 fourth-round replay win over top-flight Newcastle United entered English football folklore as arguably the greatest FA Cup shock of all time. Elsewhere in the Midlands, though, there have been many other upsets and moments of cup magic too. Telford United (in 1984) and Kidderminster Harriers (in 1994) both made it to the fifth round, and Worcestershire village side Alvechurch hold a record they will keep forever - unless the rules are changed again - after taking four replays to see off Oxford City in a qualifying round tie in 1971. Worcester City were involved in a record-breaking penalty shootout against Scunthorpe in 2014 - the same year they famously beat Coventry City. But, while the memory of that day at Hereford - Ronnie Radford et al - surpasses all other memories, across the Worcestershire border, it perhaps still irks a bit. Accompanied by fallen 1970s non-league stars Stafford Rangers, Worcestershire clubs make up three of the four non-EFL Midlands sides to have made it through to the first round proper - the Harriers plus seventh-tier duo Alvechurch and Worcester, who all face EFL clubs. How will they fare this time? Plymouth Argyle v Alvechurch 5th in League One v 6th in Southern League Premier Central (Tier 7) On paper, it looks a very tall order for Alvechurch. But not every non-league club has got an FA Cup pedigree like the Church's manager Kyle Storer. The former Bedworth United, Tamworth, Hinckley United, Atherstone Town, Nuneaton Town, Kiddy Harriers, Wrexham, Cheltenham Town, Solihull Moors, Nuneaton Borough, AFC Telford United, Kettering Town and Alvechurch player is not just a walking advert for Midlands non-league football, he has got plenty of FA Cup "previous" to be taken into consideration. "I've been very fortunate," Storer told BBC Midlands Today. "I got to the fourth round with Kiddy Harriers, when we played at Sunderland in front of 40,000. And that was having beaten Peterborough over two games with a team that had Joe Lolley, Marvin Johnson and Chey Dunkley." Kyle Storer (background) led Kiddy Harriers out for their 1-0 fourth-round defeat by Sunderland at the Stadium of Light [Shutterstock] "And, when I was at Tamworth, we won at Bournemouth [ Storer actually scored the winner] , then took Stoke to a replay. And we got Norwich at home in third round the following year." Dion Dublin and Darren Huckerby both netted twice in a 4-1 win but Storer had the last word by getting one back. Elsewhere in the Midlands, though, there have been many other upsets and moments of cup magic too. Telford United (in 1984) and Kidderminster Harriers (in 1994) both made it to the fifth round, and Worcestershire village side Alvechurch hold a record they will keep forever - unless the rules are changed again - after taking four replays to see off Oxford City in a qualifying round tie in 1971. But, while the memory of that day at Hereford - Ronnie Radford et al - surpasses all other memories, across the Worcestershire border, it perhaps still irks a bit. Accompanied by fallen 1970s non-league stars Stafford Rangers, Worcestershire clubs make up three of the four non-EFL Midlands sides to have made it through to the first round proper - the Harriers plus seventh-tier duo Alvechurch and Worcester, who all face EFL clubs. How will they fare this time? Plymouth Argyle v Alvechurch 5th in League One v 6th in Southern League Premier Central (Tier 7) On paper, it looks a very tall order for Alvechurch. But not every non-league club has got an FA Cup pedigree like the Church's manager Kyle Storer. The former Bedworth United, Tamworth, Hinckley United, Atherstone Town, Nuneaton Town, Kiddy Harriers, Wrexham, Cheltenham Town, Solihull Moors, Nuneaton Borough, AFC Telford United, Kettering Town and Alvechurch player is not just a walking advert for Midlands non-league football, he has got plenty of FA Cup "previous" to be taken into consideration. "I've been very fortunate," Storer told BBC Midlands Today. "I got to the fourth round with Kiddy Harriers, when we played at Sunderland in front of 40,000. And that was having beaten Peterborough over two games with a team that had Joe Lolley, Marvin Johnson and Chey Dunkley." Kyle Storer (background) led Kiddy Harriers out for their 1-0 fourth-round defeat by Sunderland at the Stadium of Light [Shutterstock] "And, when I was at Tamworth, we won at Bournemouth [ Storer actually scored the winner] , then took Stoke to a replay. And we got Norwich at home in third round the following year." Dion Dublin and Darren Huckerby both netted twice in a 4-1 win but Storer had the last word by getting one back. "It was voted goal of the round too," he grins. "I've had some amazing FA Cup runs but let's hope we can go and create another day to remember. Let's hope we can cause some damage. "in terms of football prospects, it's a tough one. They're flying, aren't they? But, in financial terms, then it's amazing." Colchester United v Worcester City 23rd in League Two v 17th in Southern League Premier Central (Tier7) For the younger generations, ask any Worcester City fan what the FA Cup means to them and they will bring up the 2013-14 season. City caused "Pandemonium at the Ricoh", as BBC Hereford & Worcester freelance reporter Dan Johnson excitedly put it, when they beat then League One side Coventry. Then came that 14-13 spotkicks defeat by Scunthorpe United in that astonishing, record-breaking 30-penalty shootout. City also made the first round the following season when, despite having Troy Deeney's brother Ellis in the side, they were well beaten 3-0 at Bramall Lane by Sheffield United . This is their first appearance in the first round proper since then. But, for the result that still counts as City's biggest FA Cup scalp, you have to go way back to January 1959 - and the arrival of Liverpool at their old St George's Lane home. FA Cup highlights: Liverpool lose to Worcester City City leave Worcester after 108 years It was 11 months before the great Bill Shankly arrived at Liverpool to create the legendary 'Mighty Red' machine which became kings of English football and conquered all of Europe in the 1960s, 70s and 80s. At the time, they were still in Division Two - and not promoted until 1962 after eight years in the second tier - but it's a memory that then schoolboy, Roger King, will ever forget. "The game should have been on the Saturday but it was postponed," Roger told BBC Midlands Today. "It was quite icy. "I was at school then, Christopher Whitehead Secondary Modern. The game was rearranged for the following Wednesday afternoon and the only way you could attend was to get the ticket signed by my father, to take the headmaster and he gave you permission to have the afternoon off. "I can't remember much of the game but I do remember the crowd. We got to the ground at one o'clock and didn't get in until gone two o'clock. St George's Lane was just a residential street and it was thronged with thousands. "A lot of people talk about Hereford and their notable win, but we'll never forget our win over Liverpool." Can City cause another upset on Saturday? Well, Danny Cowley's Colchester have not won since a 1-0 victory over Rochdale on 29 August - 12 games ago - and have slipped to 23rd in League Two. It might not be Liverpool or Coventry, but it would be another significant scalp for Worcester. And it was in Essex 68 years ago that their Cup heroics all began, when they drew 0-0 with Chelmsford and beat them in a first-round replay. Kidderminster Harriers v Doncaster Rovers 13th in National League v 20th in League One After early exits in the qualifying rounds over the last two seasons, when they were a sixth-tier side, regular cup fighters Kidderminster Harriers make ther first appearance in round one since losing 2-1 at home to Fleetwood in 2023 . After promotion in May, Harriers made a great start back in the fifth tier under new manager Paul Wotton. But they have now not won in eight league games - their only victory in that time coming at home to fellow Midlanders Solihull Moors in the fourth qualifying round. Now they face Grant McCann's Doncaster, who have themselves won just three league games so far this season. Is another Harriers scalp on he cards? "You always want to win your next game," Wotton told BBC Hereford & Worcester. "And we're at home. And there's no pressure on us. "I know the manager well. I've played against him many times and I've been assistant manager when he's been the manager on the opposite bench. "We're full time, so we'll have no excuses fitness-wise but they're two leagues higher than us. "It's still a big jump for us. We're a million miles from League One. "But don't let anyone ever tell you can't do anything. We'll be as committed as we possibly can." Other Midlands sides in the FA Cup first round Saturday 7 November (15:00 GMT) Crewe Alexandra v AFC Wimbledon (4th in League Two v 18th in League One) Eastleigh v Shrewsbury Town (17th in National League v 15th in League Two Newport County v Walsall (14th v 3rd in League Two) Port Vale v Scunthorpe United (19th in League Two v 23rd in National League) Sunday 8 November (12:00 GMT) Stafford Rangers v Grimsby Town (2nd in Northern Premier League West Division v 6th in League Two)

item.title: Barcelona coach Hansi Flick has unfinished business with Diego Simeone ahead of Atletico Madrid clash
item.description: Barcelona coach Hansi Flick has unfinished business with Diego Simeone ahead of Atletico Madrid clash The last few weeks have been terrible for Barcelona, starting with defeats to Real Madrid and PSG to the injury to star midfielder Rodri . But the Catalans will not let that hamper their form as they travel to the Metropolitano to face Atletico Madrid this weekend. After all, Barcelona are running the risk of losing out on the top spot in the La Liga table, if they succumb to a defeat at the hands of Atletico Madrid. Hansi Flick has unfinished business As reported by MARCA , beating Atleti and its coach Diego Simeone will be of particular importance for Hansi Flick, who has quite the history against Los Colchoneros . Flick and Simeone have quite the history between them. (Photo by Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images) During his coaching career, Flick has crossed paths with Atletico Madrid 12 times. On paper, the record favours him a lot, with the Catalans leading on wins. Of those 12 meetings, 10 have come during Flick’s time at Barça, yielding six wins, one draw and three defeats. However, the stats do not tell the whole story as two of the three victories have come in a rather painful manner for Flick and his team. The scars of last season Both the defeats, in fact, came last season. The first came in the Copa Del Rey semifinal first leg, when Atletico Madrid secured an emphatic 4-0 win to leave Barcelona all but elminated. Although the Catalans made an admirable comeback in the second half, they were unable to completely overturn the sheer magnitude of the defeat. Hansi Flick’s Barcelona were defeated twice by Atletico last season. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) The second one was even more agonising for Hansi Flick. Simeone’s side won 2-0 in the first leg of the Champions League quarterfinal at the Camp Nou, a result Barcelona were unable to overturn at the Metropolitano. This effectively put an end to Barcelona’s hopes of winning the Champions League, much to the frustration of Flick. Now, that same Atletico Madrid side, who were defeated by Bayern Munich in the Champions League, will have the opportunity to dethrone Barcelona at the top of the table this weekend. Hansi Flick, though, clearly has unfinished business and won’t let them have it easy.

item.title: “Total BS”: ESPN’s Paul Finebaum Shuts Down $10.75M SEC Coach to Replace Alabama’s Kalen DeBoer With Blunt Verdict
item.description: Paul Finebaum ripped into Lane Kiffin’s denial of an ultimatum by Ole Miss. Source: Imago ©Credit - Imago Alabama’s struggles have put Kalen DeBoer under the microscope, with questions growing about whether he is the right fit to lead one of college football’s biggest programs. As speculation over potential replacements picks up, a high-profile SEC coach has entered the conversation. But ESPN’s Paul Finebaum isn’t buying the idea, and his response makes his position fairly clear. John from St. Louis called into The Paul Finebaum Show podcast to share his thoughts on DeBoer’s future at Alabama. “My sources are telling me I have some breaking news,” John said. “I want you to try to confirm all this, but my sources are telling me that if Missouri beats Texas on Saturday and Alabama loses, then Drinkwitz is going to be offered the Alabama job. It’s going to be behind closed doors. It’s going to be kind of a double secret.” Without giving any weight to his thoughts, Finebaum completely dismissed the claim as baseless, saying no credible sources support the rumor. Finebaum's taking no prisoners on the DeBoer speculation. Stay locked into the latest SEC coaching drama and power moves with EssentiallySports. “First of all, that is total BS,” Finebaum responded. “No, you don’t have a single source in America, nor is that ever going to happen.” Drinkwitz has drawn attention as a possible replacement for several coaches. His name has circulated in previous coaching searches, including Auburn, Penn State, and Florida. Not too long ago, he was being considered to take the Florida job after Mike Norvell got fired. During Tuesday’s press conference, Drinkwitz addressed the rumors himself and said he was “not a candidate at Florida State.” Drinkwitz, who earns $10.75 million annually, has a 52-31 overall record at Missouri. His record in SEC games is 29-26. Over the last four seasons, Missouri has won 35 games out of 47, showing that the program has been relatively successful under him. The Tigers are 6-2 overall and 3-2 in SEC games. They are ranked No. 19 and are preparing to face No. 10 Texas, who are also at a 6-2 record. According to the CBS Sports CFP Forecaster, if Missouri beats Texas, its estimated probability of reaching the 12-team playoff rises to 15.9%. That’s roughly a 1-in-6 chance. Alabama is currently 6-2. After its bye week, Alabama will be traveling to Baton Rouge to play. If Alabama loses, a third loss would certainly put more pressure on the Crimson Tide. But it wouldn’t automatically end their playoff hopes, as they are ranked 5th in the CFP standings. They would still have Vanderbilt, Chattanooga, and Auburn remaining. item.title: ‘It’s not right’ – Jason Kelce thinks one aspect of College Football ‘doesn’t make sense’
item.description: Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Jason Kelce enjoyed an incredible career in the NFL with the Philadelphia Eagles, but not every player is so fortunate as to earn the kind of money the former centre did in their respective careers. The current college system was described by Kelce as ‘the Wild West’ in his latest New Heights podcast, where he was able to speak to legendary head coach Nick Saban about the current landscape in the world of College Football. The transfer portal has changed the landscape of the college scene, with colleges battling against each other financially in the race to sign specific players. It has brought into question just how committed players are to actually developing themselves, as opposed to simply chasing the highest-paying opportunity. Although Kelce is on the side of the players being granted the opportunity to earn from playing at the college level, he has also shared his concerns over the lack of commitment required from the players with the contracts they are signing. Jason Kelce does not agree with the current College Football contract situation Revenue sharing was introduced last year, which required the colleges to start compensating their student-athletes for their participation in the teams. Although there are certainly some positives to this, it is apparent that the system is far from perfect. “These kids sign contracts, but they mean nothing. They just leave. They don’t have any penalty for leaving,” Nick Saban said. https://open.spotify.com/embed?uri=spotify%3Aepisode%3A1h6N7H8Nm6nabFjSG6eijX “Well, that’s the thing that doesn’t make sense to me. Like, and I know you’ve talked to Congress and they’re trying to get this thing right, but it doesn’t make sense that there’s a commitment from the university, but no commitment in terms of like a contract or any type of time period from the player. Like it’s, you know, it’s the Wild West,” Jason Kelce responded. “It’s not right what’s going on. And it’s not in the best interest of the player, like you just said, like all for players getting paid. But, I developed so much of, you know, work ethic and all of these other attributes in college because you have to figure it out and you have to grind it. And it’d be interesting going through college nowadays, with how it happens and how quickly guys just up and leave the moment there’s any type of adversity or anything.” Kelce and Saban clearly have their concerns over the impact the financial games between colleges could have on the players’ characters as they develop towards a career in the NFL. There is an obvious feeling that chasing the money at an early age is not the example that should be set to these players. The counter argument would be that the players have to take the money whilst it is on offer to them, as the future is not guaranteed. However, it seems as if Kelce and Saban are both calling out for more commitment to be gained for the colleges through the contracts being signed by

item.title: 'We are an honest group' - Andoni Iraola reacts as Liverpool top the Premier League fouls chart before Crystal Palace trip
item.description: FBL-EUR-C1-LIVERPOOL-PRESSER - AFP Andoni Iraola has admitted Liverpool are "sometimes too honest" after a striking statistic showed no Premier League side have conceded more fouls this season. The Reds head to Crystal Palace on Sunday on the back of two straight defeats to Arsenal and Fenerbahce, and their manager wants a response, with Ryan Gravenberch still a doubt because of a heel problem. Liverpool top the Premier League for fouls conceded Liverpool have conceded 128 fouls in the Premier League this season, more than any other side in the division, as reported by The Independent. At the other end of the scale, only three teams have won fewer fouls than Iraola's side, who have been awarded just 88. The Reds have lost their last two games, against Arsenal and Fenerbahce, and were denied a penalty against the Gunners despite Alexander Isak having his shirt pulled. The topic was raised at Iraola's press conference ahead of Sunday's trip to Selhurst Park. Iraola unsure how to take referee's praise The Liverpool boss accepted that his players do not try to con officials, and revealed that their conduct had even earned praise from the referee. "We are quite an honest group, sometimes too honest," Iraola said. "Even the other day after the game, the referee congratulated us… I'm not sure if I like that or not! "Our behaviour was very good. I think it has to be genuine; you cannot fake things; it has to be genuine complaints. We are willing, we want to press, we want to be intense – but the balance is that there's a big difference." Iraola explains Liverpool's 'strange season' Liverpool sit fifth in the Premier League, nine points off leaders Arsenal. They have conceded only nine goals in nine league games, but have already let in 10 in four Champions League matches. "It's been a strange season," Iraola added. "In the Champions League, we are scoring a lot and conceding a lot. In the Premier League, we are scoring less and conceding less. We obviously want to score more, concede less! "It's a matter of controlling the games. Sometimes against Fenerbahce, we're controlling too much, having good positions and arriving but sometimes we have to throw numbers in the box. It will take away more control, yes, but it gives us more threat. Especially against Arsenal… the way we attack the box has to be better." Gravenberch a doubt as Liverpool chase Palace win Iraola confirmed that Gravenberch is touch and go for Selhurst Park as the midfielder continues to manage pain in his heel. "A week ago, we were on a run and in a good place and in a better mood," he said. "Now it changes and it has to be like this. We have to react after two defeats: we need the win against Palace away."
item.content:encoded: FBL-EUR-C1-LIVERPOOL-PRESSER - AFP Andoni Iraola has admitted Liverpool are "sometimes too honest" after a striking statistic showed no Premier League side have conceded more fouls this season. The Reds head to Crystal Palace on Sunday on the back of two straight defeats to Arsenal and Fenerbahce, and their manager wants a response, with Ryan Gravenberch still a doubt because of a heel problem. Liverpool top the Premier League for fouls conceded Liverpool have conceded 128 fouls in the Premier League this season, more than any other side in the division, as reported by The Independent. At the other end of the scale, only three teams have won fewer fouls than Iraola's side, who have been awarded just 88. The Reds have lost their last two games, against Arsenal and Fenerbahce, and were denied a penalty against the Gunners despite Alexander Isak having his shirt pulled. The topic was raised at Iraola's press conference ahead of Sunday's trip to Selhurst Park. Iraola unsure how to take referee's praise The Liverpool boss accepted that his players do not try to con officials, and revealed that their conduct had even earned praise from the referee. "We are quite an honest group, sometimes too honest," Iraola said. "Even the other day after the game, the referee congratulated us… I'm not sure if I like that or not! "Our behaviour was very good. I think it has to be genuine; you cannot fake things; it has to be genuine complaints. We are willing, we want to press, we want to be intense – but the balance is that there's a big difference." Iraola explains Liverpool's 'strange season' Liverpool sit fifth in the Premier League, nine points off leaders Arsenal. They have conceded only nine goals in nine league games, but have already let in 10 in four Champions League matches. "It's been a strange season," Iraola added. "In the Champions League, we are scoring a lot and conceding a lot. In the Premier League, we are scoring less and conceding less. We obviously want to score more, concede less! "It's a matter of controlling the games. Sometimes against Fenerbahce, we're controlling too much, having good positions and arriving but sometimes we have to throw numbers in the box. It will take away more control, yes, but it gives us more threat. Especially against Arsenal… the way we attack the box has to be better." Gravenberch a doubt as Liverpool chase Palace win Iraola confirmed that Gravenberch is touch and go for Selhurst Park as the midfielder continues to manage pain in his heel. "A week ago, we were on a run and in a good place and in a better mood," he said. "Now it changes and it has to be like this. We have to react after two defeats: we need the win against Palace away."

item.title: Braves predicted to sign $3.9M flamethrower to replace Raisel Iglesias, pair with Robert Suarez
item.description: Braves predicted to sign $3.9M flamethrower to replace Raisel Iglesias, pair with Robert Suarez originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . It is time for the Atlanta Braves to turn their attention to the 2027 season, as free agency is officially underway. Now, it is a matter of whether they can make their moves before a potential lockout. Atlanta has several important needs to address this offseason. Once again, the Braves will need to add pitching, whether that means strengthening the starting rotation or adding to the bullpen. They did a good job addressing those needs last offseason, beginning with the re-signing of closer Raisel Iglesias. “The Braves have addressed one of their offseason priorities by re-signing closer Raisel Iglesias to a one-year, $16 million contract. Atlanta announced the deal Wednesday. Iglesias, a 35-year-old right-hander, had completed a four-year, $58 million contract that paid him $16 million in each of the past three seasons,” ESPN wrote. Atlanta didn't stop with bringing Iglesias back. The team also landed one of the best closers in baseball in 2025, signing flamethrower Robert Suarez to create a formidable 1-2 punch at the back of the bullpen. “Closer Robert Suarez has signed a three-year, $45 million contract with the Atlanta Braves, the team announced Thursday. Suarez, who led the National League this season with 40 saves in 45 chances, became a free agent in early November after opting out of $8 million options for 2026 and 2027,” ESPN wrote. Bleacher Report’s Tim Kelly believes the Braves could add another flamethrowing bullpen arm by signing Adrián Morejón this winter. “There's little doubt Morejon has the stuff to pitch in the ninth inning. However, not having to be the closer might make him more appealing, because teams with established closers could still be in on him. Earlier in these predictions, we projected that Raisel Iglesias would leave the Braves because we think they could invest more in someone like Morejon,” Kelly wrote. This would be a great move for Atlanta, as Morejón was dominant in 2026 and could serve as the setup man for Suarez over the next couple of seasons. It would also mark the second consecutive offseason in which the Braves added a reliever from the San Diego Padres . Morejón played under a $3.9 million contract in 2026. Atlanta would likely have to pay a significant price to bring him aboard, but the investment could be worthwhile. Regardless of the specific moves they make, addressing the pitching staff should be the Braves' top priority this offseason. item.title: Jayson Tatum Lands Top-Five Spot in NBA's First MVP Rankings
item.description: Jayson Tatum Lands Top-Five Spot in NBA's First MVP Rankings originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Jayson Tatum is already receiving some early MVP consideration. In his first MVP ladder of the 2026-27 season, NBA.com's Shaun Powell ranked the Boston Celtics star fifth behind Luka Doncic, Victor Wembanyama, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Tyrese Maxey. "Most, if not all, of the fears about Tatum here in his first full season following an Achilles injury have subsided," Powell wrote . "The more distance he puts between that and now, the better for the Celtics, who are down a star after Jaylen Brown’s trade to Philly. "Yet Tatum is showing he can carry the load, at least so far. He’s averaging 35 minutes a night, including a pair of back-to-back games for the reigning Eastern Conference Player of the Week." MORE: Joe Mazzulla Sends Strong Message About Paul George Tatum has bounced back in a big way since scoring just 13 points in Boston's season-opening loss to the Detroit Pistons. He's now averaging 27.0 points, a career-high 7.9 assists, 6.0 rebounds and 0.7 steals per game while shooting 41.8 percent from the field. Tatum has already recorded three 30-point games, including a 40-point outing against the Brooklyn Nets that ended with him hitting a game-winning buzzer-beater in overtime. His strong start also earned him Eastern Conference Player of the Week honors for Week 2 of the season. He beat out Giannis Antetokounmpo, Scottie Barnes, Evan Mobley and Maxey for the recognition. Tatum's production has helped the Celtics get off to a 6-2 start, tying them with the Detroit Pistons for the second-best record in the Eastern Conference. item.title: Ducks land in CFP rankings despite rocky season
item.description: Oregon football’s season hasn’t worked out the way it expected. But the Ducks (5-3, 3-2 Big Ten) were ranked in the first College Football Playoff rankings. Oregon came in at No. 23 in the initial rankings, revealed live on ESPN on Tuesday. Dan Lanning’s team is on the outside looking in at the 12-team playoff, one season before a 24-team playoff is set to likely go into effect. The No. 23 Ducks are coming off a confidence-boosting win over Northwestern, heading on the road to face No. 12 Ohio State (6-2, 4-1) this Saturday. That matchup originally included the preseason Nos. 1 and 2 teams in the AP poll. But in this chaotic college football season, the Buckeyes are reeling after a road loss to No. 20 USC. Other Big Ten teams in this week’s CFP rankings include No. 19 Iowa, No. 8 UCLA and No. 4 Indiana. item.title: 3 reasons why Alabama will defeat LSU in Week 10 clash, 3 why not
item.description: Alabama heads into another hostile environment on Saturday afternoon as they travel to Tiger Stadium to take on a fellow two-loss squad in LSU. One of the headliners of a loaded Week 10 college football slate, both teams are looking to avoid a consequential third loss and to stay in the SEC race. This game could also potentially be the difference between making the College Football Playoff and missing it. That's not even taking into consideration the rivalry aspect of it between the Crimson Tide and Tigers. With everything on the line, here are three reasons why Alabama will win on Saturday, as well as three why they will not. Why: Big day from Keelon Russell There is a good chance that if Alabama is going to win this game, they are going to need a big day from Keelon Russell. LSU has statistically one of the top defenses in the SEC, however, opposing quarterbacks have been able to have some success against them. Most notably, Trinidad Chambliss threw for 363 yards with three total touchdowns against them earlier this season. Kenny Minchey also had a solid day against them in LSU's other loss. Alabama is going to need the Keelon Russell that they got against South Carolina and Mississippi State, not the one they got against Georgia and Tennessee, if they are going to go on the road and win this game. Why Not: Big day from Sam Leavitt LSU has beaten Alabama twice in the last 16 matchups, and both times they had an eventual Heisman quarterback at the helm (Joe Burrow in 2019 and Jayden Daniels in 2022 - Daniels won the Heisman the following season in 2023). Leavitt has put up some big numbers this season. He is second in the SEC with 2,173 passing yards and is tied for the conference lead in total touchdowns with 25. He also has 324 rushing yards and can make plays with his legs. If LSU is going to win, it will likely come with a big day from their quarterback. Why: Sam Leavitt turnovers For all the good stuff that Leavitt shows, he still struggles with turnovers and that is the biggest thing holding him back. He has thrown eight interceptions this season and has also lost a fumble. In LSU's two losses, Leavitt has three of his nine turnovers. With an Alabama defense that has made a living on defensive touchdowns, there is the potential for a game-breaking play from the Alabama defense. Why Not: Tiger Stadium While it is a rare non-night game in Tiger Stadium, it is still a tough place to play, especially in big games. Alabama is in the bottom half nationally in penalties per game at 7.1, and are one of the worst in the country on the road with 9.3 per game (tenth-most) away from Bryant-Denny. Three weeks ago on the road in their loss to Tennessee, Alabama was penalized 10 times for 68 yards. They have at least eight penalties in all three road games this season. Leavitt has put up some big numbers this season. He is second in the SEC with 2,173 passing yards and is tied for the conference lead in total touchdowns with 25. Why: Sam Leavitt turnovers For all the good stuff that Leavitt shows, he still struggles with turnovers and that is the biggest thing holding him back. Three weeks ago on the road in their loss to Tennessee, Alabama was penalized 10 times for 68 yards. They have at least eight penalties in all three road games this season. That problem is exacerbated, as it was against Tennessee, if starting center Racin Delgatty is unable to go . Why: Alabama's success against Lane Kiffin Alabama has had Lane Kiffin's number throughout his career. In fact, Lane Kiffin is looking for his first win over Alabama as he comes into this game 0-5 against the Tide. He went 0-4 against Alabama while at Ole Miss, and had previously lost to the Tide while at Tennessee. While this is arguably the most talented team that Kiffin has had while facing Alabama, history is on Alabama's side when facing Lane Kiffin. Why Not: LSU's pass rush LSU boasts one of the nation's best pass rushes with 34 sacks on the season. They lead the nation in both sacks per game and sack percentage . They are led by Princewell Umanmielen who ranks fifth nationally and second in the SEC with 8.5 sacks on the year. He's not the only threat for the Tigers however as Jordan Ross and Deuce Geralds both also have five sacks apiece. With the injuries Alabama is dealing with the offensive line, LSU's pass rush could have a big day and help lead the Tigers to victory. item.title: Patriots’ TreVeyon Henderson says he was hospitalized after experiencing 'unexplained neurological symptoms'
item.description: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - TreVeyon Henderson of the New England Patriots runs onto the field prior to the game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Gillette Stadium. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) Kathryn Riley via Getty Images New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson released a statement on social media Friday explaining that his absence from the team is due to “unexplained neurological symptoms” that forced him to be hospitalized. Some of his “physical functions” have also been affected. Henderson says that he was examined and while the results were “positive and reassuring,” doctors have yet to determine a cause. “Recently, I experienced an unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of unexplained neurological symptoms that required hospitalization for several days,” Henderson wrote. “During that time, I underwent extensive medical testing and evaluation. While the results of my comprehensive medical testing have come back positive and reassuring, the cause of this remains unknown and unexplainable. “I will continue working closely with specialists and physical therapists to focus on my recovery, as these symptoms have affected my strength, coordination, and some of my physical functions. I am committed to doing everything necessary to return to full health. My health and long-term well-being remain my foremost priorities.” 🙏🏽 pic.twitter.com/l52XuixPOc — TreVeyon Henderson (@TreVeyonH4) November 6, 2026 The 24-year-old Henderson suffered a high ankle sprain in Week 4 and was initially expected to miss multiple weeks. He did not miss a game as he played in New England's next two games against the New York Jets and Chicago Bears, rushing for a total of 40 yards on 10 carries. This story will be updated.

item.title: Richard Sherman predicts what San Francisco 49ers will now do with Brandon Aiyuk
item.description: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images Brandon Aiyuk is attempting to lay down the foundations for his potential return to the NFL, as his agent has revealed the wide receiver will report to the San Francisco 49ers’ training facility on Friday. Whether the Niners even let him in the building remains a totally different question. George Kittle admitted that he is not so convinced that Aiyuk will be warmly welcomed back by the organisation when he spoke to the media on Thursday. A report from Tom Pelissero claims Aiyuk now owes the Niners around $13 million in bonus forfeiture. This is something that could also complicate his return to the team over the coming days, weeks or months. Former 49ers cornerback Richard Sherman has now shared his thoughts on the situation, having previously sat in that locker room in Santa Clara. Richard Sherman shares his verdict on Brandon Aiyuk’s 49ers situation “This Brandon Aiyuk situation continues to evolve. Everybody thought it was going away. You thought it had quietened down, but he’s gotten new representation, and it’s Drew Rosenhaus. So, it sounds like he’s going to file for reinstatement for however long that takes the league to go through what they need to go through to reinstate him and then the 49ers make a decision whether to release him or keep him or whatever they do,” Sherman said on his podcast. “I know there are some cap issues if they release him immediately. I think they take on some cap hits or something like that. So, that’s what I would expect them to do. But, if it becomes too big of an issue, you know, maybe there are some alternatives that they can look into, trading him, etc. But again, the salary is prohibitive.” Given how well the Niners have started the 2026 season – currently the NFC’s top-seeded team – this situation surrounding the outcasted wide receiver is not exactly the distraction Kyle Shanahan will want around his team. The Niners’ head coach has been pretty clear in his assessment of the Aiyuk situation over recent months, and it is unlikely his stance will change. Although the Niners may take a cap hit in sending Aiyuk off away from the organisation, it is a long-term gain given the controversy and unnecessary noise he has brought to San Francisco. Liam Livingstone was part of a 4-player CSK-SRH swap deal ahead of IPL 2027 auction The IPL trading window exploded into action on November 5, 2026, as Chennai Super Kings and Sunrisers Hyderabad finalised a high-profile multi-player deal ahead of the upcoming auction. The trade saw England all-rounder Liam Livingstone and Australian fast bowler Jack Edwards head to Chennai, while Indian seamer Khaleel Ahmed and Australian pacer Nathan Ellis moved to Hyderabad. The move represents a stark divergence in roster construction strategy. Sunrisers Hyderabad prioritised bowling stability by bringing back Khaleel and pairing him with Ellis's proven death-bowling skill set. Meanwhile, Chennai Super Kings opted to sacrifice two frontline bowling options to add explosive power to their middle order, betting on Livingstone's ability to clear boundaries at Chepauk and chip in with flexible spin overs. The trade immediately divided opinion across the cricket world, with analysts questioning whether CSK diluted their bowling depth for an overseas batter who faces tough internal competition for a spot in the XI. item.content:encoded: CSK-SRH IPL 2027 trade: Liam Livingstone reacts after R Ashwin's co-host compares him to 'trash' originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Former South Africa performance analyst Prasanna Agoram (Pdogg) pulled no punches on R Ashwin's YouTube channel, comparing Liam Livingstone's trade move to getting money for trash[cite: 4]. CSK and SRH completed a major four-player trade ahead of IPL 2027, sending Livingstone and Jack Edwards to Chennai in exchange for Khaleel Ahmed and Nathan Ellis. Livingstone delivered a subtle, laughing response on social media in response to the harsh commentary surrounding his move to Chennai. Liam Livingstone was part of a 4-player CSK-SRH swap deal ahead of IPL 2027 auction The IPL trading window exploded into action on November 5, 2026, as Chennai Super Kings and Sunrisers Hyderabad finalised a high-profile multi-player deal ahead of the upcoming auction. The trade saw England all-rounder Liam Livingstone and Australian fast bowler Jack Edwards head to Chennai, while Indian seamer Khaleel Ahmed and Australian pacer Nathan Ellis moved to Hyderabad. The move represents a stark divergence in roster construction strategy. Sunrisers Hyderabad prioritised bowling stability by bringing back Khaleel and pairing him with Ellis's proven death-bowling skill set. Meanwhile, Chennai Super Kings opted to sacrifice two frontline bowling options to add explosive power to their middle order, betting on Livingstone's ability to clear boundaries at Chepauk and chip in with flexible spin overs. The trade immediately divided opinion across the cricket world, with analysts questioning whether CSK diluted their bowling depth for an overseas batter who faces tough internal competition for a spot in the XI. Amid the online chatter, Livingstone posted a subtle, light-hearted reaction on X , dropping a series of laughing emojis alongside a GIF of 'Stitch' sitting in the rain to brush off the heavy criticism. 🤣🤣🤣🤣🤣🤣🤣 https://t.co/IlCcQ7Fpgt pic.twitter.com/MYkhJbqS9o — Liam Livingstone (@liaml4893) November 6, 2026 MORE: Livingstone moves to CSK: Explaining the finances and auction purse impact Ashwin's co-host Prasanna Agoram delivers a scathing assessment of Livingstone The tactical merit of the trade was heavily debated on Ravichandran Ashwin's popular YouTube channel, which featured renowned cricket performance analyst Prasanna Agoram, widely known as "Pdogg." Agoram, who served as the Technical Strategy Analyst for the South Africa national cricket team for over a decade and has worked closely across T20 franchises, delivered a scathing evaluation of SRH releasing Livingstone to Chennai. During the breakdown, Agoram drew a brutal analogy to illustrate how SRH essentially managed to offload an unneeded asset while still extracting financial value from Chennai Super Kings. "Old clothes, unused clothes, and money for that. A person is giving money for a piece of cloth to be put in the trash. Shall we say no?" He continued, "We have tried to burn it or dispose of it somewhere. When a person is giving money for that, will you say no? They gave 13 crores and took Livingstone. I don't know why they picked him. He is one of the poorest picks in SRH because he can't play inside, and he didn't play inside. They released him," Agoram stated on the show. The panel highlighted that Chennai already manages a crowded overseas core, including Dewald Brevis, Noor Ahmad, and Jamie Overton. This means Livingstone enters the squad under immense pressure to justify his selection. From a pure roster balance perspective, Agoram argued that SRH walked away as clear winners by securing proven pacers in Khaleel and Ellis, while CSK took on a high-volatility gamble. MORE: IPL 2027 trade tracker: Complete list of all player and cash deals before the IPL 2027 mini-auction Prasanna clarifies Livingstone statement, shares apology "Hello, greetings. We posted a video about a trade, which received heavy criticism to what I said about SRH trade. That is why I am saying, when I am allowed to share my opinion, you are also allowed to share your opinion," Prasanna said in a video posted on X . "So, I wanted to clarify a few things. That is why I am sharing this video." A clarification on a reference made by @prasannalara regarding the CSK-SRH trade in our latest video. It was not directed at any particular player, nor was it intended to hurt anyone's sentiments. Full explanation. Peace! ✌️🕊️ https://t.co/as11KVZZaJ — Crikipidea (@crikipidea) November 6, 2026 "My answer on Liam Livingstone is: he can bowl off-spin, he can bowl leg-spin, he is a plus five on the field, and he is a liberating batter. But unfortunately, he has not played well in IPL and other leagues in the last two years. That is why he lost his place in England." He said it was his honest opinion and that he did not mean to hurt anyone's feelings. "If you feel that comments i have made has hurt you, my apologies but that's not the way it is meant." Livingstone primed to channel off-field scrutiny into an on-field response in IPL 2027 For Livingstone, arriving at CSK with high-profile criticism already ringing in the background is hardly a new challenge. After being acquired by Sunrisers Hyderabad for ₹13 crore in the previous auction, the 33-year-old endured an inconsistent run, with securing consistent game time and a clear role proving difficult. However, Livingstone remains one of the most destructive match-winners in modern T20 cricket when firing on all cylinders. MORE: ‘GG had an aura and never accepted mediocrity’ - Venkatesh Iyer reveals Gautam Gambhir’s high standards that helped KKR win IPL 2024 His ability to take down both spin and pace in the middle overs, combined with his dual capability to bowl both leg-spin and off-spin, offers a unique profile that CSK management believes they can maximise. Historically, csk have thrived on insulating experienced international players from external noise and handing them absolute clarity of role. If MS Dhoni and the CSK setup can unlock Livingstone's best form when IPL 2027 begins, the English all-rounder will have the ultimate platform to answer his harshest critics where it matters most. To keep up to date with all the latest sports news, opinion, and commentary, head to our social media pages on Facebook , Instagram and X (Twitter) .

item.title: Jannik Sinner to split with coach Darren Cahill, add Magnus Norman
item.description: World No. 2 Jannik Sinner (R) hired coach Darren Cahill (L) in 2022. File Photo by Alessandro Di Meo/EPA Nov. 6 (UPI) -- Italian tennis star Jannik Sinner will split with longtime coach Darren Cahill after the 2026 season, he announced Friday. The duo united in 2022. Cahill, who previously coached Andre Agassi and Simona Halep, helped Sinner achieve the world's top ranking and win five Grand Slam singles titles. "When we started working together in 2022, I was just a skinny, young Italian guy with a lot of questions," Sinner said in a video posted to his social media accounts . "You never gave me all the answers. You helped me find them myself. "You came in as one of my coaches. Pretty quickly, you became a lot more than that. Someone I could trust, someone I could rely on, a friend." Darren Cahill (not pictured) coached American tennis icon Andre Agassi (R,) as well as Italian Jannik Sinner (L). File Photo by Corey Sipkin/UPI View this post on Instagram A post shared by Jannik Sinner (@janniksin) Italian Jannik Sinner defended his Wimbledon title in July. File Photo by Hugo Philpott/UPI Sinner, 25, announced through a news release that Magnus Norman will join his team in 2027. Norman, a former world No. 2, previously worked with Stan Wawrinka, among others. Tennis coach Darren Cahill helped Jannik Sinner (pictured) win his first U.S. Open title in 2024. File Photo by Corey Sipkin/UPI Cahill coached Sinner to his first Grand Slam crown at the 2024 Australian Open. Sinner won the U.S. Open later that year. He defended his Australian Open title in 2025, when he also won Wimbledon, and defended his Wimbledon crown in July for his fifth major title. Cahill also served as Sinner's coach during his three-month suspension in 2025 after he tested positive for clostebol, an anabolic steroid. The Australian defended Sinner, touting his honesty, saying he had "no part in" the incident and "didn't intend to cheat." Jannik Sinner missed the end of the 2026 tennis season, including the U.S. Open, due to lingering right knee issues. File Photo by Larry Marano/UPI Sinner won his first Grand Slam title less than two months before his two positive tests. He parted ways with physiotherapist Giacomo Naldi and fitness trainer Umberto Ferrara later that year. He did not miss any Grand Slam appearances during his ban. "We've been through so much together," Sinner said of Cahill. "You told me you would stop after 2025, and somehow I couldn't seem to get rid of you. But the trophies aren't what I will remember the most. It's everything around them. Spaniard Carlos Alcaraz (L) beat Italian Jannik Sinner (R) in the 2025 U.S. Open men's singles final. File Photo by Larry Marano/UPI "The long hours on the practice courts, flights, the dinners, the love. Even the days when everything felt heavy, you were there for all of it. I always knew I was in good hands. Not just me, everyone who travels with us. Everyone behind the scenes. "With you, we are more than a team. You taught

File Photo by Corey Sipkin/UPI Cahill coached Sinner to his first Grand Slam crown at the 2024 Australian Open. Sinner won the U.S. Open later that year. He defended his Australian Open title in 2025, when he also won Wimbledon, and defended his Wimbledon crown in July for his fifth major title. The Australian defended Sinner, touting his honesty, saying he had "no part in" the incident and "didn't intend to cheat." Jannik Sinner missed the end of the 2026 tennis season, including the U.S. Open, due to lingering right knee issues. File Photo by Larry Marano/UPI Sinner won his first Grand Slam title less than two months before his two positive tests. He parted ways with physiotherapist Giacomo Naldi and fitness trainer Umberto Ferrara later that year. He did not miss any Grand Slam appearances during his ban. But the trophies aren't what I will remember the most. It's everything around them. Spaniard Carlos Alcaraz (L) beat Italian Jannik Sinner (R) in the 2025 U.S. Open men's singles final. File Photo by Larry Marano/UPI "The long hours on the practice courts, flights, the dinners, the love. Even the days when everything felt heavy, you were there for all of it. I always knew I was in good hands. Not just me, everyone who travels with us. Everyone behind the scenes. "With you, we are more than a team. Cahill, 61, led players to eight Grand Slam titles during his coaching tenure. That span included two title runs from Halep and Agassi's 2003 Australian Open victory.
