item.title: Bottas Reveals What Broke in His Mexico Crash, and Why Cadillac Didn’t See It Coming
item.description: Valtteri Bottas says heat from his Cadillac’s brakes caused the suspension failure that sent him into the barriers at the Mexico City Grand Prix. Bottas was braking for Turn 1 at the end of the main straight when his front-left suspension failed, and the car spun backward into the tire barrier. He climbed out on his own, and the race was red-flagged so the barrier could be repaired. Speaking to the media at Interlagos on Thursday, Bottas gave the fullest account yet of what went wrong. He also talked about his future at Cadillac, which Darshan covered here . Brake Heat Reached the Wishbones The part that failed was the mountings for the wishbones, the suspension arms that connect the wheel to the chassis. Bottas said the team has found exactly what broke and why. “These things shouldn’t happen. But again, it happened,” he said. “The main thing is we understand why. We did have certain limits when it comes to temperatures, but we’ve had to review those.” The heat came from the brakes, which are hard to cool in Mexico City’s thin, high-altitude air. “Still, the heat from the brakes, it’s got to go somewhere. And at the moment, part of it is going to the wishbones,” Bottas said. The team knew the parts got hot, but not that hot for that long. “We’re just running too long time in the red zone,” he said. “We thought it was safe, but we never tested by running it so long at that temperature.” He added that his car was running hotter than expected in Mexico, so he was already lifting and coasting to manage it when the suspension broke. What Cadillac Has Changed for Brazil Cadillac has gone back to the previous version of the wishbone mountings and lowered the temperature limits for those parts. “We’ve changed the spec to actually previous spec,” Bottas said. “It’s just the wishbone mountings. And we’ve lowered the limits, which shouldn’t be an issue here.” The suspension is now back at Silverstone, where Cadillac is stress testing it to set more accurate temperature limits. Bottas doesn’t expect a repeat at Interlagos, where Sunday should be much cooler, with maybe some rain. “If we didn’t understand what broke and why, then you would struggle with confidence. But we understand, and we know now what the limits are. So that’s why it’s okay,” he said. “Mexico is going to be the hardest one for the rest of the season with the temperatures.” The crash left him with only a bruised muscle, and he said he now feels “completely normal.” Valtteri Bottas (FIN) Cadillac Formula 1 Team MAC-26, practice day at the Mexico City Grand Prix, Oct. 30, 2026. Image Credit: Cadillac F1 Team Not Cadillac’s First Brake Problem Cadillac has fought brake overheating all through its first F1 season. In Hungary, Bottas had to put out a fire himself after his front-left brake went up in flames. Bottas said all the retirements have made it hard to judge his performance this season. item.title: Goalkeeper considers early retirement after Jesús de Miguel's death
item.description: Goalkeeper considers early retirement after Jesús de Miguel's death Goalkeeper Jesús Owono, 25, is reportedly considering retiring from professional football following the tragic collision involving Jesús de Miguel. The incident occurred in the final minutes of the match between Tenerife and FC Andorra in Spain’s second division and resulted in the Tenerife striker suffering cardiac arrest and subsequently dying. The psychological toll on the Andorra goalkeeper was revealed this Friday by Ana Maye. A former general coordinator of the Equatorial Guinea Football Federation and a close confidante of the player for 14 years, Maye described the situation in a lengthy interview with Spanish newspaper Mundo Deportivo . "No matter how much people try to comfort him, it has been incredibly difficult. He is deeply shaken, especially when he thinks about Jesús de Miguel’s widow and the one-and-a-half-year-old son he left behind. Owono doesn’t know how to cope with all of this," explained Maye, who has remained in constant contact with the player since the tragedy that shook international football. The weight of the situation has affected the goalkeeper’s entire family. According to Maye, the hostility has spread beyond social media. "People are calling Jesús’s brother a murderer, and even some parents at his team are insulting him. His sister, who studies at the University of Valencia, is also suffering terribly. They don’t deserve this. He is a man of deep faith; he reads the Bible... Nobody steps onto the pitch intending to kill a fellow player, and I hope people understand that he cannot carry that guilt." A grieving family and media pressure Owono’s mother, who lives in the Netherlands, traveled to Andorra to support her son in person. Ana Maye also criticized the way some Spanish media outlets have covered the incident, saying the exposure is worsening the family’s suffering. "They are grieving too, in a different way. Jesús de Miguel’s family has lost a loved one, and the weight of that is unimaginable. But Owono’s family’s lives have also changed forever, and they don’t deserve to have their lives destroyed by this pressure," said the player’s friend, calling for more privacy for the family, which includes younger siblings. "His mother always taught him that humanity is what makes the world go round. He needs time, psychological support and peace to process everything that has happened." Jesús Owono’s statement Last Thursday, the goalkeeper himself broke his silence in an official statement released by FC Andorra. In it, Owono expressed the impact the tragedy has had on his life. "These have been the hardest days of my life. It is very difficult to find the words or come to terms with what happened. I feel profound sorrow over the loss of Jesús. My thoughts are with him, his family and everyone who loved him," the goalkeeper wrote, indicating that he would cooperate with the proceedings surrounding the case. item.title: Europa League: How many points Milan and Juventus need to qualify
item.description: Europa League: How many points Milan and Juventus need to qualify Juventus and Milan are heading in opposite directions in the Europa League, and a new projection shows exactly how many points each will need to reach the knockout stage. According to Corriere dello Sport , data platform Football Meets Data has calculated the likely qualification marks with four games of the league phase left. Ten points should be enough to finish in the top 24 and reach the playoffs, with a 95% chance of qualifying. Nine points drops that to just 52.8%. Reaching the last 16 directly will be harder. A top-eight finish with 15 points comes with only a 50.9% chance. That rises to 89.4% with 16 points and 99.6% with 17. Goal difference could also decide places for teams level on points. ALKMAAR, NETHERLANDS – NOVEMBER 05: Teun Koopmeiners of Juventus celebrates with teammates after scoring his team’s first goal during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 match between AZ Alkmaar and Juventus at AZ Stadion on November 05, 2026 in Alkmaar, Netherlands. (Photo by Lars Baron/Getty Images) Juventus on course, Milan in trouble as Europa League heats up Luciano Spalletti’s Juventus are already on 10 points and unbeaten after Thursday’s 2-1 win at AZ Alkmaar . Teun Koopmeiners scored against his former club, and Randal Kolo Muani added a second. Two more wins would put them on the verge of the last 16. ITALY – NOVEMBER 05: Lenny Joseph of Ferencvarosi TC celebrates scoring his team’s first goal with teammate Veljko Birmancevic during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 match between AC Milan and Ferencvarosi TC at Stadio San Siro on November 05, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Milan face a much tougher task. Rúben Amorim’s side lost 2-0 at home to Ferencváros, with Lenny Joseph scoring both goals. They have just three points from four games and have dropped to 28th, outside the playoff places. They probably need at least seven points from their last four matches.
item.content:encoded: Europa League: How many points Milan and Juventus need to qualify Juventus and Milan are heading in opposite directions in the Europa League, and a new projection shows exactly how many points each will need to reach the knockout stage. According to Corriere dello Sport , data platform Football Meets Data has calculated the likely qualification marks with four games of the league phase left. Ten points should be enough to finish in the top 24 and reach the playoffs, with a 95% chance of qualifying. Nine points drops that to just 52.8%. Reaching the last 16 directly will be harder. A top-eight finish with 15 points comes with only a 50.9% chance. That rises to 89.4% with 16 points and 99.6% with 17. Goal difference could also decide places for teams level on points. ALKMAAR, NETHERLANDS – NOVEMBER 05: Teun Koopmeiners of Juventus celebrates with teammates after scoring his team’s first goal during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 match between AZ Alkmaar and Juventus at AZ Stadion on November 05, 2026 in Alkmaar, Netherlands. (Photo by Lars Baron/Getty Images) Juventus on course, Milan in trouble as Europa League heats up Luciano Spalletti’s Juventus are already on 10 points and unbeaten after Thursday’s 2-1 win at AZ Alkmaar . Teun Koopmeiners scored against his former club, and Randal Kolo Muani added a second. Two more wins would put them on the verge of the last 16. ITALY – NOVEMBER 05: Lenny Joseph of Ferencvarosi TC celebrates scoring his team’s first goal with teammate Veljko Birmancevic during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 match between AC Milan and Ferencvarosi TC at Stadio San Siro on November 05, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Milan face a much tougher task. Rúben Amorim’s side lost 2-0 at home to Ferencváros, with Lenny Joseph scoring both goals. They have just three points from four games and have dropped to 28th, outside the playoff places. They probably need at least seven points from their last four matches.

item.title: Sehwag's quickfire fifty, Ishan Sood's three-wicket haul power India U-19 to big win over Nepal in Under-19 Asia Cup opener
item.description: India Under-19 began their Under-19 Asia Cup campaign with a 10-wicket win over Nepal Under-19 on Friday, after fast bowler Ishan Sood's three-wicket spell with the new-ball set up a straightforward chase for the openers in Al Amerat, Oman. Aaryavir Sehwag and Lakshya Raichandani remained unbeaten as India chased down the target of 129 in just 19.1 overs, with 30.5 overs to spare. Sehwag scored 70 off 52 balls, hitting seven fours and four sixes, while Raichandani made 53 off 63 balls, including seven boundaries. Earlier, India captain Lakshya Raichandani opted to field after winning the toss, and Sood made an early impact with the new ball. He dismissed opener Prashiddha Jaishi (1 off 7), No. 3 batter Suryanshu Koirala (5 off 6) and No. 4 Nischal Kshetri (0 off 12) to leave Nepal struggling at 27/3 in the ninth over. Left-arm pacer Manal Chauhan then bowled Niraj Yadav to claim Nepal's fourth wicket. Darsh Sonal (43 off 93) and Aashish Luhar (29 off 45) tried to steady the innings with a 43-run partnership for the fifth wicket. However, Yashveer Goud broke the stand by dismissing Aashish, triggering another collapse. Nepal were eventually bowled out for 128 in 42.3 overs. Darsh Sonal was their highest scorer, followed by Aashish. Sood finished with figures of 3/18, while Arjun Rajput also picked up three wickets, conceding just eight runs. Goud claimed two wickets, while Kavya Paresh Patel and Chauhan took one each. India Under-19 will next face Pakistan Under-19 in their second match of the tournament on Sunday.

item.title: Alex Ferguson legacy in focus! Michael Carrick reflects on legendary boss as Manchester United prepare for Aston Villa showdown
item.description: Manchester United manager Michael Carrick has called on his players to use their midweek European heroics as a springboard for domestic consistency. Speaking ahead of a high-stakes encounter with Aston Villa, the Red Devils boss also took time to reflect on the immense influence of Sir Alex Ferguson as the club marks a major milestone for the legendary Scotsman. Honouring the Ferguson dynasty The atmosphere at Old Trafford this weekend will be charged with nostalgia as Manchester United commemorates 40 years since Sir Alex first walked through the doors of the Theatre of Dreams. Speaking to the media about the legendary manager's enduring impact, Carrick was quick to highlight how the Scotsman's arrival in November 1986 transformed the trajectory of the club forever. "It's something definitely worth celebrating as a football club, 40 years this week since he came here," the United boss explained. "I am probably closer to him, and speak more to him now, than I did when I was playing. Ever since he came here, the impact he has had on me as an individual was immense." To truly honour that history, Carrick believes his side must find the formula for sustained success rather than relying on sporadic bursts of brilliance. Managing the squad after Roma thriller While the focus is partially on the past, Carrick’s immediate concern lies with a squad that is currently balancing the highs of a Champions League comeback with the harsh realities of a growing injury list. The manager confirmed a significant blow to his midfield options, revealing that Carlos Baleba is set for a stint on the sidelines. The youngster suffered an injury during the dramatic 3-2 victory over Roma and is expected to be out for several weeks, with a return only likely following the conclusion of the upcoming international break. There was slightly more optimistic news regarding Patrick Dorgu, who is "slowly getting back" to fitness after a seven-game absence, though his involvement against Villa remains subject to late assessments. Reflecting on the midweek victory that ignited the Old Trafford crowd, Carrick was careful to ensure his players did not become complacent after the emotional high of the European turnaround. He described the result as a "one-off" and stressed that the hard work is only just beginning if the team wants to climb the Premier League table. "We scored some goals from nowhere. I thought we played really well and deserved to win the game. Nothing is done yet. It is one moment in time that we need to use to move forward. We need more of it, for sure," he told the media. item.title: Ravens might be making a huge mistake with new plans for NFL trade deadline
item.description: Ravens might be making a huge mistake with new plans for NFL trade deadline originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Baltimore Ravens are in trouble. Lamar Jackson is likely out for the rest of the regular season, and Tyler Huntley is as well. They're reportedly trading for Jacoby Brissett, but that might not be enough to salvage the season. With this major quarterback problem, it would not be a surprise if the Ravens adjusted their trade deadline plans. They have made some changes, but it's not exactly how some might've expected after losing QB1 and QB2 for the season in the same game. According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , the Ravens are not planning to sell at this year's trade deadline. Despite their playoff hopes being all but gone, the Ravens are not going to sell, which could wind up being a huge mistake. Ravens could be making a big mistake with plans not to sell at NFL trade deadline "I don't see the Ravens in sell mode," Rapoport said. "The reason why I say that is the Jacoby Brissett trade is going to be official this morning; he is going to be their starting quarterback when they take the field Monday against the Los Angeles Chargers ... So no, I do not believe the Ravens are in sell mode. I don't think they're in buy mode either." From @GMFB: Could the #Ravens be sellers at the trade deadline (no); Plus, the # Vikings will start Carson Wentz on MNF. https://t.co/VAKpk6SThK — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) November 6, 2026 The Ravens are swinging a trade for Brissett as a temporary resolution to their quarterback problem, but it's hard to believe this team will have much of a chance to win anything this season. Instead, the Ravens should look to trade away players at this year's trade deadline. Losing Jackson and Huntley for the season is a very strong indicator that their season is over. Sure, Brissett might help the Ravens to a win or two throughout the rest of the season. But it's really hard to imagine that this team will be good enough to win anything, especially after how defeated they looked on Thursday Night Football in Week 9. MORE : Why it's time for Colts to move on from Shane Steichen and Daniel Jones The Ravens are now 4-5 on the season, and firmly in last place in the AFC North. Brissett would have to play extremely well for this Ravens team to have any chance of making the playoffs. But even if they did make it there, it's hard to imagine Brissett leading this team on any sort of playoff run. So, with that in mind, the Ravens should really look to sell. They don't have to trade someone like Derrick Henry, as he's in their long-term plans. But players on expiring contracts or veterans who have shaky futures with the team should be readily available. Rashod Bateman, Marlon Humphrey, Chidobe Awuzie, Calais Campbell, Justice Hill, and even someone like Mark Andrews should be available for trade. This season is likely a wash, so the Ravens should be selling. I

item.title: Quinshon Judkins Will Dominate Fantasy for the Next Few Weeks
item.description: Cleveland Browns running back Quinshon Judkins runs the ball against the Pittsburgh Steelers | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Cleveland Browns are looking to avenge last week's loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers, and star running back Quinshon Judkins will play a crucial role in the game-plan this week. Cleveland is set to go on the road to take on the New Orleans Saints, and Judkins is garnering attention as a key contributor for Week 9 fantasy football lineups. He struggled last week against a dominant Steelers front, tallying just 25 rushing yards over 11 carries, adding two catches for 24 yards in the passing game. The week prior, though, Judkins flashed his fantasy ceiling in a matchup against the Tennessee Titans. He posted a season-high 96 rushing yards over 17 carries, taking on encouraging workload near the goal line with two rushing touchdowns for the afternoon. Judkins closed Week 7 ranked as RB3 in PPR for the week, notching a 23.4 fantasy points, another season-high mark. Quinshon Judkins at Titans: 17 CAR 96 YDS 2 TD His third career game with 2+ rush TD. pic.twitter.com/kQQIKKzNzD - StatMuse (@statmuse) October 25, 2026 I expect Judkins will re-capture this caliber of production against New Orleans, and he's building a case to dominate fantasy football for the next few weeks. Quinshon Judkins Will See Expanded Role Alongside Shedeur Sanders Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders hands off the ball to Cleveland Browns running back Quinshon Judkins | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Cleveland Browns are pivoting at the quarterback position, with starter Deshaun Watson set to miss Week 9 due to a concussion. Second-year signal-caller Shedeur Sanders is set to handle the reins under center for Cleveland, which will likely present expanded volume for Judkins and the run game. Browns QB Deshaun Watson did not practice again Thursday while he remains in concussion protocol; Shedeur Sanders is in line to start Sunday vs. the Saints. - Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 5, 2026 Coming into a favorable matchup against New Orleans, an uptick in workload will help Judkins replicate his RB3 finish from Week 7. He's struggled to carve out consistent efficiency, averaging just 3.4 yards per carry so far this season, but an expanded role should remedy such a concern. Cleveland's offense will feature a steady rushing attack throughout the course of Sunday's game, elevating Judkins' fantasy ceiling heading into a notably favorable matchup. Las Vegas enters its respective Week 9 matchup ranked 31st in run defense, while Cincinnati is ranked as the No. 20 unit against the run. Houston will present a tough matchup, but has struggled at times against the run, allowing 294 rushing yards over its last two games. item.title: Turkey to push for 'electrification' drive at COP31 as climate threats mount
item.description: COP31 host Turkey is set to push for a "electrification" drive to help meet global elergy demand as the UN climate conference kicks off in Antalya on Monday. The annual summit takes place this year under the shadow of a cost-of-living crisis fuelled by the war in the Middle East.

item.title: The Fifa hopeful hoping to take Infantino down with 'samurai spirit'
item.description: [Getty Images] Kozo Tashima is under no illusions it will be easy to take down Gianni Infantino - but the first serious challenger for the Fifa presidency says he will draw on his "samurai spirit". First, the 68-year-old needs to get the endorsement of five member associations around the world. The honorary president of the Japan Football Association said he has had "good replies" from those he has contacted since announcing his ambition to run in the March elections. If he achieves the necessary endorsements, the next step is an altogether different proposition - toppling Infantino, who has been in charge of Fifa for a decade and told BBC Sport last month he believed he had the backing of the "vast, vast majority" of world football. Tashima, who sits on the Fifa Council, acknowledged the scale of the challenge, but wants to bring "good change" to the organisation. The former footballer says he is driven by disappointment in Infantino's recent actions, surrounding the cancelled suspension of United States forward Folarin Balogun at the World Cup and the abandoned plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors. In an exclusive interview with BBC Sport, he spoke of why he feels he cannot leave Fifa as it is. "I know [Infantino] has a lot of supporters," he said. "Now I am alone and my budget is not enough but it is OK. My policy, my philosophy, I have to fight against him with my samurai spirit. "I would like to make sure that the game of football is safeguarded and to be loved and enjoyed by everybody. We have to review the system in Fifa and build good governance. "In the uncertain situation of the world, sports - especially football - can present good values like fair play, co-operation, hard work, integrity, and show the model of the society. So, first to review and rebuild good governance and make football accessible for all with the principle of football first." I already asked to some of the member association and [received] good replies so far." He laughed when asked if he realistically hopes to win the election in Morocco in March, before saying: "Of course, of course yes, I hope I will win. It is not easy." Tashima's campaign will centre on his philosophy for the role of Fifa president, which he described as one based on the "values of sincerity, soundness, fair play, and integrity". Regarding the Balogun red-card incident, which involved US President Donald Trump calling Infantino to ask for the ban to be reviewed, Tashima said: "I have never seen the red card and the next game who can play. "In the uncertain situation of the world, sports - especially football - can present good values like fair play, co-operation, hard work, integrity, and show the model of the society. So, first to review and rebuild good governance and make football accessible for all with the principle of football first." Japan's Tashima to stand against Infantino for Fifa presidency Fifa to share 'key documents' over World Cup sell-off plan Infantino says he is backed by 'vast majority' Asked how confident he was in his ability to get the five endorsements, he said: "I have confidence. I already asked to some of the member association and [received] good replies so far." He laughed when asked if he realistically hopes to win the election in Morocco in March, before saying: "Of course, of course yes, I hope I will win. It is not easy." Tashima's campaign will centre on his philosophy for the role of Fifa president, which he described as one based on the "values of sincerity, soundness, fair play, and integrity". Regarding the Balogun red-card incident, which involved US President Donald Trump calling Infantino to ask for the ban to be reviewed, Tashima said: "I have never seen the red card and the next game who can play. "This is, I hope, never happens in the world football. He didn't explain about this issue, how to come and how [it came] to happen. He added: "Most of the things are not answered yet by Mr President Infantino. "With my experience in Japan Football Association, Asian Football Confederation, and Fifa, for some more than 20 years, I would like to bring good change if I am elected." Last month, former Tottenham Hotspur defender Ramon Vega announced his intention to stand as a candidate in next year's Fifa presidential election. He told BBC Sport he had received "more than five" endorsements, but declined to give details of the identities of the member associations backing him. All candidates must prove they have played an "active role" in football for two of the last five years. Vega has said he is confident he is eligible to stand for the presidency as a shareholder of a club. Vega has attempted to run for the presidency three times before but each time has failed to garner the necessary support of five associations. Tashima can therefore be considered the first serious challenger to Infantino. item.title: Ben Roethlisberger says Steelers RB Jaylen Warren belongs in MVP conversation
item.description: (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s hard to put into words just how important Jaylen Warren has been to the Steelers’ success this season. The running back’s 998 scrimmage yards through eight weeks of action is good for third in the league behind only Jahmyr Gibbs and Jaxon Smith-Njigba. There is no doubt that Warren is playing at an elite level, and people are starting to have some serious conversations about the way the back has been playing. Former Steelers quarterback Ben Roethlisberger recently went as far as to say that Warren deserves MVP consideration for his play so far this season on his “Footbahlin with Ben Roethlisberger” podcast. “This guy needs to start to be talked about in some MVP stuff. Like league MVP or offensive MVP,” Roethlisberger said. “His numbers and some of the stuff he’s doing is pretty impressive. His yards after contact have to be some of the highest in the league. There’s a lot of things that don’t look good and then all of a sudden it’s like, oh, he fell forward for three.” Warren is averaging 4.89 yards per touch so far this season, the most by any running back with at least 100 touches. Despite his incredible efficiency and performance this season, there are still 16 players with higher odds to win the NFL’s Offensive Player of the Year award on FanDuel Sportsbook. Is Warren a value play? Possibly, but the clear reason for the lack of love for Warren comes from the fact that he only has three touchdowns this season. Despite being a workhouse and the best player on Pittsburgh’s offense, the touchdown output, coupled with the Steelers not being a flashy offense, hurts his chances significantly. All of this to say that Roethlisberger is absolutely correct in saying Warren deserves significantly more attention than he is getting for the unbelievable season he is in the midst of having for the Steelers. item.title: How to get Poké Ball Pattern Vivillon in Pokémon Legends: Z-A
item.description: Game Freak and The Pokémon Company are distributing a Poké Ball Pattern Vivillon in Pokémon Legends: Z-A , now that players have worked hard enough to unlock it. It's the first time in 10 years that pattern of Vivillon has been available, and all you need to do to get it is claim it from Mystery Gift. Scatterbug and Spewpa are comparatively easy to get early in Legends: Z-A , though this one is special.
item.dc:creator: Josh Broadwell
item.content:encoded: Game Freak and The Pokémon Company are distributing a Poké Ball Pattern Vivillon in Pokémon Legends: Z-A , now that players have worked hard enough to unlock it. It's the first time in 10 years that pattern of Vivillon has been available, and all you need to do to get it is claim it from Mystery Gift. Scatterbug and Spewpa are comparatively easy to get early in Legends: Z-A , though this one is special.

item.title: Arteta confirms Saka out for 'weeks', Konsa fit
item.description: Bukayo Saka will be sidelined for "weeks" by a quad injury (Karl-Josef HILDENBRAND) Mikel Arteta said Friday that Arsenal winger Bukayo Saka would be out of action for "weeks" but had a positive message about the fitness of defenders Ezri Konsa and William Saliba. Saka was forced off with a quad injury during Arsenal's 2-2 draw against Bayern Munich last month and was left out of Thomas Tuchel's squad for upcoming England matches. "We're talking about obviously weeks, let's say after the international break," Arsenal boss Arteta said ahead of the visit of Hull to the Emirates Stadium on Saturday. "He's going to start hitting the pitch and start to have more activity and see how he feels, but unfortunately he's going to be out for a while." Konsa was taken off during a 2-1 win at Slavia Prague on Wednesday but is fit to face Hull. The former Aston Villa defender was recruited in August, partly to provide cover for Saliba during his prolonged absence with a back injury. Saliba returned to the squad for the first time this season for the trip to Prague but did not play. Arteta, whose team are top of the Premier League, said he would not stand in the way if coach Zinedine Zidane calls up Saliba to the France squad. "They have all the information. Now it's about them, about Zinedine in this case, to give the call," said Arteta. "We will accept whatever it is. It's more between them because William needs minutes as well." He added: "I know how much he loves to be around the national team. It's a new manager, a really exciting one as well, so whatever he's decided is fine for us." Despite the absence of Saka, Tuchel's squad includes five Arsenal players -- Ben White, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Eberechi Eze, Declan Rice and Konsa. "It is a proud thing to have a big English core in the national team," said Arteta. "Our club, it is something that is part of our identity. They are super happy to be back, you can see that. Let's focus on tomorrow and then after that they can go and do their bit with the national team." kca/jw/gj

item.title: Warriors’ Jimmy Butler’s lively sideline antics vs. Heat draw obvious relationship analogy
item.description: Credit: Kelley L Cox-Imagn Images Warriors’ Jimmy Butler’s lively sideline antics vs. Heat draw obvious relationship analogy appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Jimmy Butler couldn’t hide his excitement during the Golden State Warriors ’ 120-100 victory over the Miami Heat, and teammate Georges Niang had a hilarious explanation. The injured star, who has been working toward his return from a torn ACL, was particularly animated on the sideline against his former team. Speaking after the win, Niang addressed Butler’s lively behavior, joking that the forward probably had extra motivation against Miami. “I wonder why,” Niang said when asked about Butler’s energy. He then offered a relationship analogy to explain the competitive feelings that can linger after leaving a team. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Do you want to see your ex do better than she was with you? Not really.” Niang, who has played for several NBA teams, admitted he understands wanting to prove something against a former organization. He also joked that Butler was probably listening to country music and screaming in the weight room. Beyond the jokes, Niang praised Butler’s character and generosity behind the scenes. He recalled how Butler welcomed teammates to San Diego home and continued checking on them despite his injury. Niang revealed that Butler even offered him help while recovering from his torn ACL, something that genuinely surprised the veteran forward. Butler’s enthusiasm also followed his playful Instagram trolling after the Heat victory, adding another entertaining chapter to his reunion with Miami. Although Butler remains sidelined, Niang’s comments highlighted how the Warriors star continues supporting his teammates while maintaining his trademark humor. His presence has provided Golden State with another source of leadership, showing that Butler remains invested in the team’s success even while facing a lengthy recovery. Related: Warriors’ Draymond Green fires back at Dillon Brooks by calling out ‘de-escalate’ BS after recent skirmish Related: Warriors star Stephen Curry reveals Steve Kerr’s message after 0-3 start that sparked win streak

item.title: Daily Slop: Why Jayden Daniels is next-level protecting the ball (via Washington Post)
item.description: The Daily Slop – 6 November 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Washington Post (paywall) How Jayden Daniels turned protecting the football into his ‘superpower’ Through all of the Commanders’ struggles, the quarterback has remained one of the NFL’s most efficient passers. Ahead of his freshman year of college in 2019, Jayden Daniels sat down with then-Arizona State coach Herm Edwards. The quarterback had been an excellent decision-maker in high school, but the former NFL coach wanted to drill home that the margin for error was about to shrink. He figured that Daniels had a future playing on Sundays and wanted to prepare him for what would come next. “He always told me, ‘No matter what, you give yourself a chance to win the game if the possession always ends with a kick,’” Daniels told The Washington Post. “Whether that’s a punt or a field goal, you always want to end it with a kick.” That was ingrained in Daniels throughout his five years of college football, and it hasn’t changed in the slightest through his third season with the Washington Commanders. Among the 33 NFL quarterbacks who’ve attempted at least 100 passes this season, he’s the only one who hasn’t committed a turnover. Few quarterbacks have been better than Daniels at protecting the football since he entered the NFL in 2024. He has an interception rate of just 1.5 percent (the fourth lowest among quarterbacks who attempted at least 500 passes during that span). Overall, he’s committed just 14 turnovers (tied for the fewest). “You just got to be locked in for six seconds each play,” Daniels said. “It kind of just goes with the flow of the game. And then, also, just having that discipline of like, ‘Okay, if it’s not there, don’t force it.’” To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Sports Illustrated Commanders Mailbag: Is Luke McCaffrey Being Overlooked? Did Dan Quinn Win Back Trust? With Terry McLaurin out for the year, McCaffrey’s limited role on offense is harder to overlook. Plus, what the Eagles win did—and didn’t—change for Dan Quinn. item.content:encoded: The Daily Slop – 6 November 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Washington Post (paywall) How Jayden Daniels turned protecting the football into his ‘superpower’ Through all of the Commanders’ struggles, the quarterback has remained one of the NFL’s most efficient passers. Ahead of his freshman year of college in 2019, Jayden Daniels sat down with then-Arizona State coach Herm Edwards. The quarterback had been an excellent decision-maker in high school, but the former NFL coach wanted to drill home that the margin for error was about to shrink. He figured that Daniels had a future playing on Sundays and wanted to prepare him for what would come next. “He always told me, ‘No matter what, you give yourself a chance to win the game if the possession always ends with a kick,’” Daniels told The Washington Post. “Whether that’s a punt or a field goal, you always want to end it with a kick.” That was ingrained in Daniels throughout his five years of college football, and it hasn’t changed in the slightest through his third season with the Washington Commanders. Among the 33 NFL quarterbacks who’ve attempted at least 100 passes this season, he’s the only one who hasn’t committed a turnover. Few quarterbacks have been better than Daniels at protecting the football since he entered the NFL in 2024. He has an interception rate of just 1.5 percent (the fourth lowest among quarterbacks who attempted at least 500 passes during that span). Overall, he’s committed just 14 turnovers (tied for the fewest). “You just got to be locked in for six seconds each play,” Daniels said. “It kind of just goes with the flow of the game. And then, also, just having that discipline of like, ‘Okay, if it’s not there, don’t force it.’” To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Sports Illustrated Commanders Mailbag: Is Luke McCaffrey Being Overlooked? Did Dan Quinn Win Back Trust? With Terry McLaurin out for the year, McCaffrey’s limited role on offense is harder to overlook. Plus, what the Eagles win did—and didn’t—change for Dan Quinn. Luke McCaffrey looked good on that long kickoff return, but he barely played on offense. With Terry out for the year, is there a reason he still isn’t getting more opportunities at receiver? Question from Nigel F. via email That’s a great question that I’ve written about here before . From what I can tell, the staff likes McCaffrey, or he wouldn’t be on the roster, but he somehow keeps falling outside of the group that gets the main share of the offensive snaps at receiver. Against Philadelphia, McCaffrey played just three offensive snaps. Antonio Williams played 50, Treylon Burks 40, and Stefon Diggs 39. The team loaded up at receiver this offseason, giving the staff options even after McLaurin went down. The receiver room may not be big on names outside of McLaurin and Stefon Diggs, but rookie Antonio Williams is emerging fast , and whenever Treylon Burks can stay healthy, he routinely produces. Add in the attention tight end Chig Okonkwo gets, and there’s not much left for McCaffrey, Dyami Brown, or Van Jefferson. On film, McCaffrey gets open, so offensive coordinator David Blough has to make the scheme work with the talent they have. With injuries playing a factor, McCaffrey will likely get his shot to show what he brings to the field before the end of the season. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE The Athletic (paywall) Commanders’ grand offensive transformation remains a work in progress The Washington Commanders didn’t start over completely after their 2025 season ended with only a handful of wins. A month after the team moved on from its previous coordinators, coach Dan Quinn reintroduced David Blough, previously the assistant quarterbacks coach, as his new play caller and they laid out their basic vision of the offense. Blough’s would be “an aggressive, balanced attack,” Quinn said, with more under-center formations and a departure from the no-huddle system Jayden Daniels had grown accustomed to over the past two years. It would require the young quarterback to get comfortable with relaying play calls — some of them lengthy — then quickly reading the defense to make any checks at the line of scrimmage. Among the more noticeable changes: Daniels would work under center more and no longer operate almost exclusively from the shotgun formation. “I think it opens up some different schemes in the run game, some things that I believe in,” Blough explained in February. “It opens up different play actions and keepers and getting him on the perimeter in different ways. I think there’s a level of communication that happens under center. … I think a lot of teams that you saw even playing deep into the playoffs, it was something that was a foundation of what they did.” The goal, both Quinn and Blough said, was to create a more explosive system that would take advantage of Daniels’ accuracy and running without asking him to do everything for the offense. Throughout the offseason, Blough, a first-time play caller, collaborated with his assistants and sought the input of his players as they built a system they said would be exclusively theirs. The foundation was an amalgamation of the offenses Blough ran during his years as a quarterback, and drawing from the offenses run by Washington’s previous play caller, Kliff Kingsbury, as well as Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell and even Louisville coach Jeff Brohm, whom Blough played for at Purdue. The crux of the Commanders’ offense, however, would draw from Ben Johnson, Blough’s former coordinator in Detroit who has since transformed the Chicago Bears’ offense with his heavy use of play action, multiple tight end sets, outside zone run concepts and pre-snap motion. To read more of this story, click here Last Man Standig (paywall) OFF SCRIPT: Austin Ekeler wasn’t sure he’d play again. He was OK with that. The Commanders running back opens up about nearly retiring after tearing his Achilles, AI’s upside and scary possibilities, growing up in rural Colorado and the NFL statistic he treasures most. ASHBURN, Va. — Austin Ekeler thought he had reached the finish line of his playing career. Not necessarily while lying on the Lambeau Field grass in pain after tearing his right Achilles. But soon after the non-contact injury in Week 2 that ended his 2025 season, any quiet time became a mental battle. “I’m probably done,” Ekeler thought. “Probably retiring.” The entire picture of his work and life put the injury into perspective. The running back was a workhorse for much of his seven-year stint with the Chargers. He helped the Washington Commanders reach the NFC Championship Game in season 8. Then Ekeler tore his Achilles in Year 9. He would be 31 if he returned. 2025 was also the first year he became a father. Ekeler and his wife, Melanie, welcomed a baby boy into the world that May. The guy who grew up on a farm in rural Northern Colorado was already busy “ripping projects,” from coding to creating apps to business and real estate investing. He loves football, but it’s not his life. And yet… “I told myself, ‘Look, let’s focus on the rehab. Don’t focus on whether I’m done or not. Don’t make that decision while I’m emotional. Continue to rehab, and then once that’s done, let’s get back in shape.” Ekeler is a gym guy, so he would get back into shape regardless. “Then, if I start to feel good and people are calling about me, I’ll do a workout. If they want to have me in, great. If not, let’s go rip some more code and build some more projects. That’s what it was for me.” The calls did come. The Carolina Panthers checked in and were set to add Ekeler to their practice squad when Washington raised the stakes with a spot on the active roster. For more from

item.title: Braves Must Fix Shortstop Hole Before Vegas Meetings Start
item.description: USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect The Atlanta Braves season is over, but the real work starts right now with a glaring hole at shortstop. Battery Power reported on November 5 that the team needs a new shortstop and asked fans if any options catch their eye. This isn’t a minor fix; it is the single biggest move the front office must make before the season begins again. The roster has gaps, and the clock is already ticking on the free agent market. While the team figures out the lineup, they have secured stability on the dugout bench. Battery Power noted on November 4 that the Braves set to return their entire coaching staff for 2027. Keeping the same coaches gives the players a solid base to build on while the front office hunts for new bats and arms. This continuity matters more than people think when you are trying to win a division title. The Shortstop Void The need at shortstop is the most urgent issue facing the franchise. Battery Power listed several options and asked fans to weigh in on who they want to see in the lineup. The team cannot win a championship with a weak spot in the middle of the diamond. They need a player who can hit and field at an elite level. The options are out there, but the Braves must act fast to get the best one. Prospects like Tate Southisene and Briggs McKenzie are making waves in the Arizona Fall League. Battery Power reported that both players made the AFL Fall Stars Game, which shows the farm system has depth. However, the major league team cannot wait for kids to be ready if they want to win now. The big league roster needs an immediate upgrade, not a hope for the future. Awards and Money Talk The offseason comes with plenty of awards to hand out and money to discuss. Battery Power mentioned that the Rookie of the Year announcement drops on November 9, and Didier Fuentes likely will not win. The Manager of the Year vote comes on November 10, with Matty Mattingly, Pat Weiss, and Craig Murphy as the top names. These awards are fun to talk about, but they do not put runs on the board. Financial reports also came out ahead of a potential lockout. The Braves released their third quarter 2026 financial reports, and the numbers show the team is ready to spend. Salary cap and floor rules are always a hot topic for fans. The front office has the money to fix the shortstop spot, so there is no excuse for them to sit on their hands. What Happens in Vegas The real action starts next week when the MLB General Manager Meetings kick off on November 9 in Las Vegas. Battery Power reported that these meetings usually set the groundwork for trades and free agent evaluations. A small chance exists for minor additions to happen right then, but the big deals will start here. The Braves need to be aggressive in the room to get the player they need.

Battery Power listed several options and asked fans to weigh in on who they want to see in the lineup. The team cannot win a championship with a weak spot in the middle of the diamond. They need a player who can hit and field at an elite level. The options are out there, but the Braves must act fast to get the best one. Prospects like Tate Southisene and Briggs McKenzie are making waves in the Arizona Fall League. Battery Power reported that both players made the AFL Fall Stars Game, which shows the farm system has depth. However, the major league team cannot wait for kids to be ready if they want to win now. The big league roster needs an immediate upgrade, not a hope for the future. Awards and Money Talk The offseason comes with plenty of awards to hand out and money to discuss. Battery Power mentioned that the Rookie of the Year announcement drops on November 9, and Didier Fuentes likely will not win. The Manager of the Year vote comes on November 10, with Matty Mattingly, Pat Weiss, and Craig Murphy as the top names. These awards are fun to talk about, but they do not put runs on the board. Financial reports also came out ahead of a potential lockout. The Braves released their third quarter 2026 financial reports, and the numbers show the team is ready to spend. Salary cap and floor rules are always a hot topic for fans. The front office has the money to fix the shortstop spot, so there is no excuse for them to sit on their hands. What Happens in Vegas The real action starts next week when the MLB General Manager Meetings kick off on November 9 in Las Vegas. Battery Power reported that these meetings usually set the groundwork for trades and free agent evaluations. A small chance exists for minor additions to happen right then, but the big deals will start here. The Braves need to be aggressive in the room to get the player they need.

item.title: Why Omarion Miller's breakout game for ASU could come against former team
item.description: Towards the end of practice on Nov. 3, right after Arizona State senior wide receiver Omarion Miller finished talking to local reporters, there was a fun moment between Miller and his teammate, senior safety Adrian “Boogie” Wilson. Wilson is one of the more lively characters on the roster, and this moment was an example of that. Pretending to be a reporter himself, Wilson began to ask Miller questions ahead of this weekend’s home game against Colorado on Nov. 7 . The first one was in jest, with Wilson asking, ‘Who is your favorite teammate?’ Miller responded, ‘Probably Boogie Wilson.’ Then Wilson got into the meat of his questions. “‘What’re you most excited for playing your former team?’” Miller responded quickly. “‘To beat ‘em real bad.’” The answer was short but came with conviction. Miller is set to go against the same team he suited up for from 2023 to 2025. While Miller did his best not to provide Colorado with bulletin board material, it’s only natural to feel more pressure going against your former team. “You're going to feel something, right?” coach Kenny Dillingham said. “People are going to take that and potentially twist that. They twist everything. But you can't say no. But you can't say yes. Every person is going to handle things different. “I know he's been the same guy this week for us, same attitude, same everything. You wouldn't know the difference. But there has to be something in your head, right? That's human nature.” Miller still has a bunch of friends that he keeps in contact with in Boulder, but not for this week. It’s a place where Miller saw himself grow up, maturing into a leader for younger players in his time with the Buffaloes. “Man, I ain't gonna lie, this week I'm pretty excited going against my old team,” Miller said. “A lot of emotions going on right now, for sure. I played there for three years, going against my former team; those were my guys. Anxious to get on the field and ball.” And ball he might. While Miller did his best not to provide Colorado with bulletin board material, it’s only natural to feel more pressure going against your former team. “You're going to feel something, right?” coach Kenny Dillingham said. “People are going to take that and potentially twist that. They twist everything. But you can't say no. But you can't say yes. Every person is going to handle things different. “I know he's been the same guy this week for us, same attitude, same everything. You wouldn't know the difference. But there has to be something in your head, right? That's human nature.” Miller still has a bunch of friends that he keeps in contact with in Boulder, but not for this week. It’s a place where Miller saw himself grow up, maturing into a leader for younger players in his time with the Buffaloes. “Man, I ain't gonna lie, this week I'm pretty excited going against my old team,” Miller said. “A lot of emotions going on right now, for sure. I played there for three years, going against my former team; those were my guys. Anxious to get on the field and ball.” And ball he might. It’s been an up-and-down season for Miller, who started off with eight receptions for 102 yards and one touchdown in the season opener — but that was against lower-level competition, FCS Morgan State. Miller, a priority target in the transfer portal for ASU, recorded five receptions for 85 yards and one touchdown against Baylor, although that came in a 55-19 blowout loss, one of the worst of the Dillingham era. Miller just broke a three-game spell without a touchdown by hauling in a 20-yard score to cut the lead to 17-10 against BYU on Oct. 31. The senior wide receiver feels like he’s on the verge of a breakout game — “Most definitely,” he said with a smile — and so do his coaches. “It's close,” Dillingham said. “Last week there were multiple opportunities that (if) one of those balls is caught, that's his breakout game. There it is, just one of those four or five other opportunities. It's going to happen. It's just a matter of when, because we're all around it, we're dancing with it.” Heading into the season, Miller and fellow transfer Reed Harris, coming over from Boston College, knew it was unlikely they were both going to have huge seasons. So far, it’s been Harris (48 receptions for 804 yards and eight touchdowns) who has broken out and is gaining traction as a first-round NFL draft pick. “Coming here, both of us knew we both couldn't be the guys,” Miller said. “So we knew one of us was gonna have to be lower than the other one.” Scouting report: How Arizona State football and Jake Fette can beat Colorado Many thought it would be Miller, who was ranked No. 2 in the transfer portal among wide receivers. But Miller has taken it all in stride and is happy for his teammate. Miller said that probably wouldn’t have been the case a few years ago. “As a young guy, I probably would not be happy,” Miller said. “That's part of learning as a college player. When it’s all said and done, we’re a team. I’m always happy for any one of my teammates. Whether they're doing good or bad, I stay motivated now, and they stay motivating me. We stay on each other so we can all do our best.” Defenses are starting to zero in on Harris, with BYU sending a safety at Harris at the start of each snap for most of the game. Miller is hoping to use that to his advantage. “They just want to double Reed,” Miller said. “They forgot I'm still on the team.” It’s been a quarterback carousel for ASU this season, with freshman Jake Fette now helming the offense after sophomore Cutter Boley began the year as the starter and then was replaced by senior Mikey Keene. A knee injury to Keene paved the path for Fette. While it’s early on, Miller can feel the connection between him and Fette growing. “It’s coming along really good,” Miller said. “I feel like Jake knows the skill set of our receivers. I always tell him, ‘Throw it in the air, and we gonna make you look good.’” Miller’s on the cusp of showing why the Sun Devils targeted him so quickly in the transfer portal, and it may poetically come against the team he left for ASU. item.title: Will Falcons’ James Pearce Jr. play vs. Bengals in Week 9 after 8-game suspension?
item.description: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Will Falcons’ James Pearce Jr. play vs. Bengals in Week 9 after 8-game suspension? appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Atlanta Falcons will be playing against the Cincinnati Bengals this week, and there is a chance one of their players won’t be on the field. After serving an eight-game suspension, James Pearce Jr . was eligible to return this week, but he’s also dealing with a back injury that the team is monitoring, according to team reporter Tori McElhaney. “A change to the injury report: RB Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) has been ruled OUT. James Pearce Jr. is dealing with a back issue that the Falcons will monitor throughout the weekend, per Kevin Stefanski,” McElhaney wrote on X, formerly Twitter. The Falcons are hoping that they can get Pearce back so they can get a boost on the defensive end, specifically getting pressure on the quarterback. They’ve been fine at doing so throughout the season, but Pearce brings another level that they can help them become even better in that category. He showed that last season in his rookie year when he finished with 10 1/2 sacks. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “I see it as a positive to add a good player to the mix,” Stefanski said via Daniel Fick of the Atlanta Journal-Constitution. “I think the way ‘Brick’ and the defensive staff have constructed this rush plan, obviously married up with the coverage plan, I think it’s beneficial to all parties to do your job. But adding another good player to the mix is a good thing.” James was suspended for eight games for violating the league’s personal conduct policy after he was arrested in February due to an altercation with his ex-girlfriend. He was charged with aggravated battery with a deadly weapon, fleeing and eluding police and resisting an officer with violence to his or her person. Related: Falcons adjust Week 9 injury report for Bengals game in Madrid with Brian Robinson Jr. downgrade Related: Falcons’ Bijan Robinson shoots down notion that he is NFL’s best RB, for now

item.title: This see-through camera lets photographers maintain eye contact with their subjects
item.description: Lutra, a South Korean startup, has debuted a new brand called Humans of Authenticity (HOA) that's launching another screen-free digital camera that incorporates a large open viewfinder into its design, as spotted by PetaPixel . The camera is reminiscent of the Godox C100 but the HOA A1 positions its lens and sensor close to the center of its large viewfinder window so that a photographer can maintain eye contact with their subject, or feel more in the moment while framing a shot without staring at a screen. item.title: 5 Buccaneers players to watch vs. Bears
item.description: There is arguably no team in the NFL hotter right now than the Chicago Bears , and fans are in for another prime-time showdown this weekend as they get set to welcome the Tampa Bay Buccaneers to town for Sunday Night Football. The Bears (6-2) are winners of three in a row after they traveled to the Pacific Northwest and defeated the reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks 34-17 in one of the best regular season victories in recent memory. Quarterback Caleb Williams was able to move the ball unlike previous quarterbacks against Seattle's defense, while running back D'Andre Swift capitalized with three rushing touchdowns. Meanwhile, defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons had a debut that will be remembered for years to come as he stifled the Seahawks offense for much of the game. As for the Buccaneers (3-5), they have climbed their way out of the NFC South basement and are back on tracking following the return of quarterback Baker Mayfield. Tampa has won three of their last four games and is coming off a historic 16-0 win over the Atlanta Falcons, where they didn't complete a single pass in monsoon conditions. Despite their poor record, the Buccaneers have a formidable defense, and their offense can get things going with their impressive ground attack. Here are five Buccaneers players we'll be watching this Sunday night: 1. QB Baker Mayfield It's been two weeks since Baker Mayfield returned to action following an injury to his right hand, and he hasn't had to do a whole lot. During Tampa Bay's two-game winning streak, Mayfield has completed just seven of 14 passes for 64 yards and a touchdown. He made history last week by not completing a single pass in the Buccaneers' win over the Falcons, which is a nice soft restart to his season. Don't expect that to be the case Sunday, though. The Bears' defense will be too good to allow Tampa to solely rely on their rushing attack to carry the load. Mayfield will likely have his most passing attempts since late September against a Bears defense that can suddenly now get after the quarterback more effectively. We'll see how healed his thumb is and whether or not he can get after this Bears secondary that has a proponent for giving up big passing plays. 2. item.content:encoded: There is arguably no team in the NFL hotter right now than the Chicago Bears , and fans are in for another prime-time showdown this weekend as they get set to welcome the Tampa Bay Buccaneers to town for Sunday Night Football. The Bears (6-2) are winners of three in a row after they traveled to the Pacific Northwest and defeated the reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks 34-17 in one of the best regular season victories in recent memory. Quarterback Caleb Williams was able to move the ball unlike previous quarterbacks against Seattle's defense, while running back D'Andre Swift capitalized with three rushing touchdowns. Meanwhile, defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons had a debut that will be remembered for years to come as he stifled the Seahawks offense for much of the game. As for the Buccaneers (3-5), they have climbed their way out of the NFC South basement and are back on tracking following the return of quarterback Baker Mayfield. Tampa has won three of their last four games and is coming off a historic 16-0 win over the Atlanta Falcons, where they didn't complete a single pass in monsoon conditions. Despite their poor record, the Buccaneers have a formidable defense, and their offense can get things going with their impressive ground attack. Here are five Buccaneers players we'll be watching this Sunday night: 1. QB Baker Mayfield It's been two weeks since Baker Mayfield returned to action following an injury to his right hand, and he hasn't had to do a whole lot. During Tampa Bay's two-game winning streak, Mayfield has completed just seven of 14 passes for 64 yards and a touchdown. He made history last week by not completing a single pass in the Buccaneers' win over the Falcons, which is a nice soft restart to his season. Don't expect that to be the case Sunday, though. The Bears' defense will be too good to allow Tampa to solely rely on their rushing attack to carry the load. Mayfield will likely have his most passing attempts since late September against a Bears defense that can suddenly now get after the quarterback more effectively. We'll see how healed his thumb is and whether or not he can get after this Bears secondary that has a proponent for giving up big passing plays. 2. RB Bucky Irving If the Bears are going to stifle the Buccaneers offense, they need to contain running back Bucky Irving. And this is a homecoming Irving is likely looking forward to. The 2024 fourth-round pick out of Hazel Crest is playing in his first game in Chicago since turning pro, and he's coming off a career day. Irving totaled 170 rushing yards on 27 carries last week and scored a touchdown in Tampa's win over Atlanta. The rushing yards and carries were both career highs, and it was Irving's third game in four weeks with over 100 rushing yards. He is the engine that is powering the Buccaneers' offense and will be the focal point that the defense needs to hone in on. Irving could have a long day, though, considering the Bears' defense hasn't allowed 100 yards rushing in a game since Week 3 and is allowing the fourth-fewest yards per game (86.8). 3. C Graham Barton A big reason the Buccaneers' run offense has been so effective as of late has been because of Graham Barton's improved play. The third-year center has been one of the better centers as of late, becoming a problem for opposing defensive lines. He was hitting key blocks all day long against the Falcons to help the Buccaneers rush for 324 yards, and he did so while battling the flu. Barton will likely be much closer to 100% this weekend, and the Buccaneers will need him to be. He'll be squaring off against Jeffery Simmons, who terrorized the Seahawks offensive line just a few days ago. The Buccaneers offensive line as a whole is strong with Tristan Wirfs and Luke Goedeke anchoring the tackle positions, but Barton's level of play has taken them to a new level. It will be interesting to see how he handles an improved Bears defensive line. 4. DE Reuben Bain If you asked 10 Bears fans who they were hoping to land in the 2026 NFL Draft, the vast majority would have said defensive end Reuben Bain, fully knowing there was little to no shot he would be available to them at pick No. 25. They will get to see him in action, though, as one of Tampa's edge rushers, and he faces a tall task in going against Darnell Wright. Bain, the No. 15 overall pick in the draft, had a slow start to his NFL career but has picked things up in recent weeks. Over his last three games, Bain has totaled one sack, one tackle for loss, and seven pressures. Bain is a smaller edge rusher, and concerns about his arm length were prevalent throughout the pre-draft process. Those concerns could come into play against Wright, who is a hulking right tackle and has allowed just 12 pressures and one sack all year. 5. LB Alex Anzalone Bears fans know Alex Anzalone all too well from his days with the Detroit Lions. The veteran linebacker left Detroit in the offseason for Tampa Bay and was having a quiet season before breaking out for a career day last Sunday. Anzalone was responsible for two of Falcons quarterback Michael Penix's four interceptions, both coming in the first quarter. That put him to three on the year, which nearly matches his career total coming into the season (four). While it's highly unlikely Anzalone has a repeat performance against a quarterback that has thrown just 14 interceptions in two and a half seasons, his familiarity with the Bears and head coach Ben Johnson could prove useful for the Buccaneers defense. Anzalone only went up against the Bears once last season when he was with the Lions, and that was back in Week 2. Much has changed since then. He will be the field general for the defense and try to counteract Williams, something that is becoming increasingly more difficult for defenders. item.title: KPop Demon Hunters on 4K Blu-ray costs less than a month of Netflix Premium
item.description: Buying the 4K Blu-ray disc version of KPop Demon Hunters was already going to be a wise idea for some people, especially those who primarily keep their $26.99 Netflix Premium subscription just to watch the hit animated flick in 4K. But at just $24.99 from Barnes and Noble instead of its original $49.95 price, it’s easier than ever to recommend. One important thing to note: it’s unavailable to ship from Barnes and Noble, but you can find a discounted copy at most retail stores, and the site makes it easy to reserve a copy online to pick up later. Amazon was matching the price earlier today, but is currently offering a slightly less tempting deal. KPop Demon Hunters (4K Blu-ray) Where to Buy: $49.95 $37.99 at Amazon $49.95 $24.99 at Barnes & Noble (in-store pickup) The Criterion Collection version of the film recently launched, and comes with a bunch of extras in a gorgeous set. In addition to the 4K digital master, complete with Dolby Vision HDR and Dolby Atmos sound, you also get two standard 1080p Blu-rays, one containing the film, and the other packed with special features (a full feature-length animatic, a making-of documentary, lyric videos, and more). It includes physical goodies, too, like collectible postcards, as well as an essay by Polygon alum Karen Han. Kpop Demon Hunters was on my list of physical movies to buy, and this deal just turned it into a must-buy ahead of the holiday season.

item.title: Meet Nigeria’s Tracy Richards among Miss Globe 2026 Top 11
item.description: By Sekinat Osundiji Nigeria’s representative at the Miss Globe 2026, Tracy Richards, has finished among the top 11 finalists at the international beauty pageant held in Phuket, Thailand. Richards also won the Head-to-Head Challenge and secured a place in the top 25 of the talent competition at the 23rd edition of the pageant, which concluded on Friday, November 6, 2026. Vietnam’s Nguyen Thu Thao emerged as the winner, while Thailand’s Suttida Iadpoo and Ukraine’s Mariia Zheliaskova finished as first and second runners-up, respectively. Richards hails from Ohaji/Egbema Local Government Area of Imo State. She is a high-fashion model and entrepreneur who co-owns a modelling agency. Beyond modelling, she is also involved in initiatives aimed at expanding opportunities for children in underserved communities through her advocacy project, Open Horizons. The initiative focuses on providing children in underserved communities in Lagos with access to mentorship, education and experiential learning through after-school programmes and educational outings. According to the project, the initiative is founded on the belief that exposing children to new experiences and opportunities can help shape their aspirations and future. Reacting to her performance, Richards’ team, in a post on Instagram on Friday, celebrated her top 11 finish and appreciated Nigerians who supported her throughout the competition. “From the moment she stepped onto the international stage in Phuket, Thailand, Tracy carried the Nigerian spirit, grace and determination with pride. What a journey, what a beautiful representation, and what an achievement to celebrate!” the team said. Thanking supporters who voted and encouraged the contestant, the team added, “To everyone who voted, supported, encouraged and stood behind her throughout this journey, THANK YOU.” It further described her performance as a source of national pride, saying, “Tracy, you made Nigeria proud. Your journey does not end here, and your light will continue to shine.” Her top 11 finish, victory in the Head-to-Head Challenge and placement among the top 25 in the talent competition marked a notable outing for Nigeria at the international pageant. Vanguard News The post Meet Nigeria’s Tracy Richards among Miss Globe 2026 Top 11 appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: DoJ's 'Super Intelligence Task Force' up and running
item.description: The US Department of Justice (DoJ) says its Super Intelligence Task Force (SINTF) is now up and running, after president Donald Trump ordered the move in a memo last month. Headed up by director of national intelligence Jay Clayton, as well as associate attorney general Stanley Woodward and associate deputy attorney general Stephen Weiss, SINTF's responsibility is to protect the US's lead in artificial intelligence development. Thursday's announcement, which was littered with the " super intelligence " Trumpism, said the task force will ensure the US's SI/AI leadership remains uncompromised by foreign AI "abuse," including by state and state-backed groups, criminal enterprises, individuals, or corporate entities. Per Trump's October 13 memo [PDF], SITF will take "affirmative measures, as appropriate," to ensure the US stays ahead in AI development. It did not elaborate on what this nebulous phrase meant, but it can be reasonably assumed this means a breadth of proactive steps. The memo also stated that the task force will organize the DoJ's criminal and civil lawsuits involving AI, recommend enforcement priorities concerning public safety and AI misuse, develop prosecution guidance for unlawful AI conduct, and feed into legislative proposals to prevent "burdensome regulation." Addressing a Wall Street Journal tech conference this week, Pentagon CTO and SITF vice chair Emil Michael said the team would release details about its AI regulatory landscape later this month. The task force will also shoulder various cross-departmental responsibilities, such as "deconflicting investigations, cases, and other matters" among departments and the offices of US attorneys. According to quotes from senior officials, chief among the concerns facing ordinary US citizens are AI attacks that target individuals, as well as those that aim to disrupt critical infrastructure and other national security interests. "The creation of the DOJ-SITF marks an important moment for the Department to help advance SI technologies and, at the same time, protect American innovation," said Weiss. "The Department also has a responsibility to utilize law enforcement tools at our disposal to deter improper use of SI, harden regular reporting on SI risk and response, and ensure companies exercise vigorous internal controls so that SI technology behaves as intended. The Department is committed to protecting all Americans and our business interests." Trump compelled the US to start using the term "super intelligence" in September, claiming "artificial intelligence," the widely used and original term coined in the mid-1950s, was a better descriptor for the technology's capabilities. The US government's dedicated website for SI states that "America is in a race for Super Intelligence. We intend to win it." It also highlights a number of initiatives the government has taken to promote its AI supremacy, including legal guidance to streamline federal approvals, leading to more data centers being
item.dc:creator: Connor Jones
item.content:encoded: The US Department of Justice (DoJ) says its Super Intelligence Task Force (SINTF) is now up and running, after president Donald Trump ordered the move in a memo last month. Headed up by director of national intelligence Jay Clayton, as well as associate attorney general Stanley Woodward and associate deputy attorney general Stephen Weiss, SINTF's responsibility is to protect the US's lead in artificial intelligence development. Thursday's announcement, which was littered with the " super intelligence " Trumpism, said the task force will ensure the US's SI/AI leadership remains uncompromised by foreign AI "abuse," including by state and state-backed groups, criminal enterprises, individuals, or corporate entities. Per Trump's October 13 memo [PDF], SITF will take "affirmative measures, as appropriate," to ensure the US stays ahead in AI development. It did not elaborate on what this nebulous phrase meant, but it can be reasonably assumed this means a breadth of proactive steps. The memo also stated that the task force will organize the DoJ's criminal and civil lawsuits involving AI, recommend enforcement priorities concerning public safety and AI misuse, develop prosecution guidance for unlawful AI conduct, and feed into legislative proposals to prevent "burdensome regulation." Addressing a Wall Street Journal tech conference this week, Pentagon CTO and SITF vice chair Emil Michael said the team would release details about its AI regulatory landscape later this month. The task force will also shoulder various cross-departmental responsibilities, such as "deconflicting investigations, cases, and other matters" among departments and the offices of US attorneys. According to quotes from senior officials, chief among the concerns facing ordinary US citizens are AI attacks that target individuals, as well as those that aim to disrupt critical infrastructure and other national security interests. "The creation of the DOJ-SITF marks an important moment for the Department to help advance SI technologies and, at the same time, protect American innovation," said Weiss. "The Department also has a responsibility to utilize law enforcement tools at our disposal to deter improper use of SI, harden regular reporting on SI risk and response, and ensure companies exercise vigorous internal controls so that SI technology behaves as intended. The Department is committed to protecting all Americans and our business interests." Trump compelled the US to start using the term "super intelligence" in September, claiming "artificial intelligence," the widely used and original term coined in the mid-1950s, was a better descriptor for the technology's capabilities. The US government's dedicated website for SI states that "America is in a race for Super Intelligence. We intend to win it." It also highlights a number of initiatives the government has taken to promote its AI supremacy, including legal guidance to streamline federal approvals, leading to more data centers being built. The pivot toward renaming the technology in all official capacities raised confusion at the time. A somewhat contradictory move, the Trump administration heavily promotes its own AI innovators, but in one swoop essentially antiquated the trading name of arguably its most recognizable AI lab, OpenAI. One financier previously floated the idea that Trump ordered the shift to boost the value of .si domain names , many of which have recently been registered using MAGA-related terms and resold for millions of dollars. There is no categorical evidence that the investments are linked to the Trump family, however. ®

item.title: Apple has a secret list of banned autocomplete phrases including ‘dictator Trump’ and ‘covid is a hoax’
item.description: A researcher found over 100,000 words and phrases in "every major language" that are blocked from autocomplete and swipe-type in iOS, Reuters reports. The researcher, Derik Kauffman, says you can still type the words on the blocklist one letter at a time. But they won't pop up as predictive text suggestions and iOS's keyboard may automatically alter them when swipe-typing, like changing "left wing conspiracy" to "left wrong conspiracy." Kauffman posted the full list online , including the individual lists for different languages. Most of the words and phrases on the list are offensive, slurs, or related to topics like sex and drugs. But it … Read the full story at The Verge.
