item.title: Four dead, 14 critically ill after suspected herbal poisoning in Benue
item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi At least four persons have reportedly died, while 14 others are receiving treatment in hospital after consuming a suspected poisonous herbal mixture purchased in Oju township, headquarters of Oju Local Government Area of Benue State. The incident reportedly followed the sale of herbal preparations by three men identified as Alhaji Mai Magamani, Mohamed and Musa Kolo to residents of the Igede community during the Ihiejwo market day in Oju last weekend. An eyewitness said the incident came to light on Monday, November 2, 2026, after several residents who had purchased and consumed the herbal preparations began experiencing similar symptoms. According to the eyewitness, the first victim reportedly died on Tuesday morning, while the second died in the early hours of Wednesday. Two others subsequently died on November 4. The source added that more than 14 other persons were receiving treatment, with several reportedly in critical condition. The three men allegedly involved in selling the herbal preparations were reportedly apprehended by the Igede Youth Council in collaboration with the Oju Local Government Area Township Youth leadership and handed over to the police. The eyewitness said the Oju Divisional Police Headquarters had transferred the case to the Benue State Police Command for further investigation. Speaking during the handover of the suspects, President of the Igede Youth Council, Comrade John-Frank Ozzidi, called on the Benue State Government to ensure a thorough investigation and that anyone found culpable was brought to justice. Ozzidi said members of the community had resisted taking the law into their own hands, choosing instead to allow the police and other relevant authorities to handle the matter. He urged political officeholders from the area to monitor the investigation to ensure that the circumstances surrounding the deaths were established and justice served. Contacted, Chairman of Oju Local Government Council, Mr Jackson Ominyi, confirmed the incident but said he had yet to establish the exact number of fatalities. He said three deaths had been reported to him as of the previous day, while other affected persons were receiving treatment at the General Hospital, Oju. “My people are working on that. My security secretary, secretary and the security adviser are on it. “The others are in the General Hospital, Oju. My health department is also taking care of them. I have tried to calm the situation down. The person selling the herbs has been arrested and sent to Makurdi three days back,” he said. Efforts to reach the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Peter Aondongu, for comments were unsuccessful, as he did not respond to enquiries as of the time of filing this report. The post Four dead, 14 critically ill after suspected herbal poisoning in Benue appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: China keeps a close eye on US midterm shake-up
item.description: The US midterm elections have resulted in the Democratic Party taking control of both chambers of the US Congress, leaving Donald Trump as a lame duck president for the remainder of his term. Professor Steve Tsang of the SOAS China Institute tells FRANCE 24 that, while a weakened Trump could strengthen Beijing's negotiating position, the Chinese leadership is aware that Congress has relatively little sway over foreign policy and is keen to maintain warm personal ties between the two presidents.

item.title: FG’s ₦50,000: Step-by-step guide on how MTN users can access funds
item.description: MTN subscribers selected for the Federal Government’s ₦50,000 monthly relief programme can check their eligibility and access the financial support through the MoMo Payment Service Bank (PSB) USSD code. The National Emergency Relief and Stabilisation Intervention (NERSI) is designed to provide financial assistance to vulnerable Nigerian households to help them meet essential needs amid rising living costs. According to the official NERSI portal, beneficiaries are selected using verified national identity records and the National Social Register. Selected beneficiaries are contacted through approved payment providers, including MoMo PSB, ALAT by Wema Bank, NairaGram, OPay and Moniepoint. For eligible MTN subscribers assigned to MoMo PSB, the designated USSD code is * 671 *0#. How MTN subscribers can check eligibility and access the ₦50,000 support 1. Dial the USSD code: MTN subscribers can dial 671 0# using their registered phone numbers and follow the prompts to check their eligibility or payment status. 2. Accept the offer: Subscribers who receive an official notification confirming their selection should follow the instructions provided to give consent and accept the support. 3. Respond to MoMo notifications: Beneficiaries who receive a genuine MoMo notification requesting consent should follow the prompts and select the appropriate option to authorise the payment. 4. Open a MoMo account: Selected beneficiaries without an existing MoMo wallet can dial *671# or download the official MoMo NG app to register. 5. Access the funds: Once the ₦50,000 is credited, beneficiaries can withdraw or transfer the money through the MoMo application, USSD service or an authorised MoMo agent. They can also transfer the funds to their bank accounts. The Federal Government has explained that beneficiaries will receive SMS notifications from their assigned payment providers requesting consent before the money is transferred to their mobile wallets. In an October 30 statement announcing the commencement of the intervention, the Minister of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction, Dr Bernard Doro, said eligible beneficiaries would receive ₦50,000 monthly to support their essential needs. “Beneficiaries will receive an SMS from one of these providers asking for their consent. This message is genuine. Once consent is given, payment is made directly to the beneficiary’s account/mobile wallet,” Doro stated. The minister also clarified that beneficiaries do not need to apply, pay any fee or register through an agent to receive the support. The ministry has warned Nigerians against sharing their personal identification numbers (PINs) and Bank Verification Numbers (BVNs) with unauthorised individuals. Meanwhile, the NERSI portal states that the intervention is free and that selected beneficiaries are being contacted in batches. Subscribers whose eligibility status shows “NOT SELECTED” should note that the government has not guaranteed that everyone excluded from the current batch will receive the support in subsequent phases. item.title: Hera probe gets 1st good luck at asteroid system clobbered by NASA's DART mission | Space photo of the day for Nov. 6, 2026
item.description: null The Didymos binary asteroid system, as seen by Europe's Hera probe. The main asteroid, Didymos, dominates the frame while just a sliver of its "moonlet," Dimorphos, is visible beneath it. ESA released this image on Nov. 5, 2026. (Image credit: ESA) The European Space Agency 's (ESA) Hera spacecraft has gotten its first close-up look at the Didymos binary asteroid system. If that system sounds familiar, it's because it made headlines in September 2022 when NASA's DART (Double Asteroid Redirection Test) spacecraft smashed into it. The aim of the DART mission was to test whether an impact could divert an asteroid away from a collision course with Earth. The purpose of Hera is to follow up on DART by making up-close observations of the Didymos system. "The first thing we said was, 'Wow,'" Hera Principal Investigator Patrick Michel said in a statement about the image, which ESA released on Thursday (Nov. 5). "This is the other side of Didymos from the one that DART’s camera showed us shortly before impact, so this feels like looking at a whole new world." What is it? The Didymos system consists of the eponymous 2,560-foot-wide (780 meters) space rock and its "moonlet" Dimorphos, which is about 530 feet (160 m) in diameter. The DART mission impacted Dimorphos on Sept. 26, 2022, with the aim of causing a change in the orbital period of the moonlet. And it worked: Before the impact, Dimorphos completed one lap around Didymos in around 11 hours and 55 minutes. The DART collision reduced the length of this period by around 33 minutes. The change is a result of the fact that Dimporphos is now traveling at around 2.7 millimeters per second more slowly than it did before the collision. The newly released photo shows Didymos in detail. Just a sliver of Dimorphos is visible, below and slightly to the left of the main asteroid. Why is it incredible? The changes caused by DART were small. But in a real Earth-threatening scenario, even such a tiny shift could help divert an asteroid on a collision course — as long as scientists get enough advance warning of its approach. Hera's observations should help reveal what other changes have occurred on and around Didymos. Scientists are already seeing that, while Didymos has the same central ridge along its equator as before the impact, many changes have occurred. This includes the creation of multiple boulders, craters, and patterns of grooves or ridges. "Since we expect a lot of impact-ejected material to have made it across the approximately 1 kilometer [0.62 miles] of space from Dimorphos to Didymos, it may be that some of these characteristics originate from this transport of material, and we have exciting work ahead of us to sort it out," said Michael Kueppers, ESA’s Hera mission scientist. "We look forward to seeing much more of both bodies and systemically mapping all the changes we identify." Stay tuned to Space.com for more Hera findings from Didymos.

item.title: Pope Leo embarks on Latin America trip with a first stop in Uruguay

item.title: Football Daily | You want proper football? Here are the FA Cup first-round ties to look out for
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! For the FA Cup, the early rounds are the juice. The first round proper to be played out over the long weekend is looking, well, proper. And on Saturday at 3pm GMT, a proper time, 31 ties will kick off. No VAR, either. At the stage when the bottom two Football League divisions join the competition, focus remains on those non-league clubs fighting for the honour of the pyramid … John Aloisi winning or choking​ the Chinese Super League , a league so ‘super’ that nine of all 16 clubs in it started the season on negative points due to ‘match-fixing, gambling and corruption’ by the way, and the league leaders not even scoring a single goal in seven hours, is really not something to lay upon someone with a bad hangover. Apropos of nothing, if anyone has any objections to my views on the Chinese Super League, please address any correspondence to: Mr K Mbappé, Madrid (there’s no point two of us getting into trouble)” – Noble Francis. As a man of a certain age frequently being reminded of how out of date I am, the recent readers’ letters regarding technical solutions to shirt-pulling (Football Daily letters passim) concerns triggered distant memories. In late 1991 I was working in the Patents Advice Centre, Newcastle Central Library. A gentleman asked for help to possibly patent an ‘invention’: a football shirt with the seams held together by Velcro, so that any tug would ‘open’ the seam and provide clear evidence to the referee of illegal cloth gathering. As I helped him search for possible equivalent innovations in our paper database (yes kids!) we chatted amiably until I asked how he had come to this seemingly simple yet brilliant innovation. He paused, reddened and began to exhale with elevated pressure: ‘Did you see Arsenal the other night? Tony Adams? Disgraceful. It should never be allowed! In fact, with this shirt it won’t be, and Arsenal will have to learn to defend decently!’ Happy memories, obviously irrelavant to the modern game” – Garren Mulloy. Not fair! Bias! (Picture me, arms wide out, mouth open, eyebrows as high as they’ll go, appealing for reason.) I wrote about skin-tight shirts the other day and you ignored it, publishing a Velcro alternative. Now you’ve published another letter about skin-tight shirts ( yesterday’s letters ), days later. And it gets letter o’ the day! What’s the literary equivalent of kicking the keeper’s water bottle in frustration? I’ve just done that” – Ken Muir. I see that Celtic finally moved up the Bigger Vase charts on Thursday night and started playing a tune when their subs Osmand, Durán and Donovan came on. Too corny but my wife actually laughed at this” – Hugh Jamieson. That was a topsy-turvy Durán Durán show at Celtic, but what else would you expect from a bunch of Wild Bhoys?” – Peter Oh. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: California governor to grant clemency to all 548 death row inmates in state

item.title: FG steps up CNG push with fuel station revival, staff vehicle conversion
item.description: —Initiative promotes cheaper energy, attracts private investment — Perm Sec – –Says 10 JAC vehicles, Villa shuttle buses already CNG-hybrid By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA–The Federal Government has renewed its drive to promote the adoption of Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) with the reopening of a former petrol filling station at the State House, Abuja, now converted into a CNG refuelling facility. Plans are also underway to extend vehicle conversion services to interested government personnel. The Permanent Secretary, State House, Temitope Fashedemi, stated that the initiative underscored the administration’s resolve to lead by example in promoting cost-effective and cleaner energy alternatives, while encouraging private-sector participation in the development of the country’s gas infrastructure. Speaking at the inauguration of the facility in Karu, Abuja, Fashedemi disclosed that the project was executed through a partnership between the State House, the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles (Pi-CNG & EV), and Rollin Energy Limited, with no expenditure incurred by the State House for its rehabilitation. He explained that the Federal Government deliberately made the abandoned facility available for conversion to demonstrate the viability of the presidential initiative and encourage private investors to take advantage of emerging opportunities in the CNG market. He further explained the initiative is also aimed at addressing concerns over the limited availability of CNG refuelling stations, which has continued to constrain wider adoption of the alternative fuel. Fashedemi said government’s responsibility was to create an enabling environment for private-sector participation rather than take over the business of establishing and operating commercial refuelling facilities. He urged business operators and prospective investors to partner with Pi-CNG to establish more stations and vehicle conversion centres across the country. “All the filling stations you see around, are they owned by government? No. They are owned by people and business operators. The earlier existing and prospective business people recognise this as an opportunity and partner with Pi-CNG to establish these facilities, the better,” he said. The Permanent Secretary disclosed that the State House had already commenced the integration of CNG technology into its vehicle fleet, with about 10 recently acquired JAC vehicles being hybrid models, alongside some shuttle buses operating within the Presidential Villa. He said the government was taking further steps to encourage interested State House personnel to convert eligible personal vehicles to CNG-hybrid systems in the coming weeks. “We are demonstrating that we are walking the talk of Mr President. item.dc:creator: Nwafor
item.content:encoded: —Initiative promotes cheaper energy, attracts private investment — Perm Sec – –Says 10 JAC vehicles, Villa shuttle buses already CNG-hybrid By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA–The Federal Government has renewed its drive to promote the adoption of Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) with the reopening of a former petrol filling station at the State House, Abuja, now converted into a CNG refuelling facility. Plans are also underway to extend vehicle conversion services to interested government personnel. The Permanent Secretary, State House, Temitope Fashedemi, stated that the initiative underscored the administration’s resolve to lead by example in promoting cost-effective and cleaner energy alternatives, while encouraging private-sector participation in the development of the country’s gas infrastructure. Speaking at the inauguration of the facility in Karu, Abuja, Fashedemi disclosed that the project was executed through a partnership between the State House, the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles (Pi-CNG & EV), and Rollin Energy Limited, with no expenditure incurred by the State House for its rehabilitation. He explained that the Federal Government deliberately made the abandoned facility available for conversion to demonstrate the viability of the presidential initiative and encourage private investors to take advantage of emerging opportunities in the CNG market. He further explained the initiative is also aimed at addressing concerns over the limited availability of CNG refuelling stations, which has continued to constrain wider adoption of the alternative fuel. Fashedemi said government’s responsibility was to create an enabling environment for private-sector participation rather than take over the business of establishing and operating commercial refuelling facilities. He urged business operators and prospective investors to partner with Pi-CNG to establish more stations and vehicle conversion centres across the country. “All the filling stations you see around, are they owned by government? No. They are owned by people and business operators. The earlier existing and prospective business people recognise this as an opportunity and partner with Pi-CNG to establish these facilities, the better,” he said. The Permanent Secretary disclosed that the State House had already commenced the integration of CNG technology into its vehicle fleet, with about 10 recently acquired JAC vehicles being hybrid models, alongside some shuttle buses operating within the Presidential Villa. He said the government was taking further steps to encourage interested State House personnel to convert eligible personal vehicles to CNG-hybrid systems in the coming weeks. “We are demonstrating that we are walking the talk of Mr President. In the next few weeks, a number of our staff will be bringing their vehicles here for conversion, subject to the eligibility of the vehicles,” he said. Fashedemi, however, explained that not all vehicles were suitable for conversion, stressing that technical assessments would be conducted to determine those that met the required specifications. He described Nigeria’s abundant natural gas resources as an opportunity that had remained largely underutilised, noting that wider adoption of CNG would provide motorists and commercial transport operators with a cheaper alternative to petrol and diesel. He recalled that the removal of petrol subsidy by President Bola Tinubu, although accompanied by economic adjustments and initial public concerns, was also intended to accelerate the transition towards alternative energy sources. Fashedemi further disclosed that the new facility had undergone a trial period during which CNG was dispensed free of charge to motorists in the surrounding area for more than a week before its formal inauguration and commencement of commercial operations. The Chief Executive Officer of Rollin Energy Limited, Mubarak Umar Danbatta, said the project demonstrated the benefits of collaboration between government and private-sector operators. He explained that the facility was an integrated refuelling unit, with its compressor, dispenser and other essential equipment housed in a single system. Its double-nozzle dispensers allow vehicles to refuel from both sides. According to him, the station has the capacity to serve approximately 150 vehicles daily, including motorbikes, depending on cylinder sizes and operating pressure. Danbatta said the State House project was the company’s second partnership with Pi-CNG, following an earlier collaboration inaugurated on May 29, 2024. He disclosed that Rollin Energy currently operates facilities in Ilorin and Abuja, while two additional stations in Kano are expected to be commissioned next week, with another two planned for Kaduna. The company, he said, is targeting nearly 15 CNG refuelling facilities nationwide by the end of 2026. Meanwhile, the Chairman of Pi-CNG, Barrister Ismael Ahmed, said the Federal Government was targeting 2,000 additional CNG refuelling stations to accelerate the adoption of alternative fuel nationwide. He disclosed that 106 stations were currently operational, while another 170 were at various stages of development or awaiting regulatory approvals. Ahmed said President Tinubu had directed the establishment of 1,500 additional stations in February and another 500 in August, with the projects expected to come on stream between this year and early 2027. He described the programme as having moved beyond the experimental stage, stressing that the priority was now to expand infrastructure at a scale capable of meeting the demands of Nigeria’s estimated 220 million population and 12 million vehicles. On the impact of the initiative, Ahmed said CNG-powered buses had reduced transportation fares by between 30 and 40 per cent on routes where they were operating, including Abuja, Lagos and the Kano-Katsina corridor. He disclosed that commuters who previously paid between N3,000 and N4,000 on the Kano-Katsina route could now travel for approximately N1,500 using CNG-powered buses. In a related development, the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Domestic Affairs, Toyin Subair, said the Federal Government and state governments were expanding investments in CNG-powered buses, trucks, tricycles and other mass transit vehicles to ensure that the benefits of cheaper fuel translated into reduced transportation costs. Subair disclosed that the National Economic Council had committed to a joint financing arrangement with the Federal Government to support the deployment of affordable transportation solutions across the states. He said the administration was targeting a reduction of 40 per cent or more in transport fares, particularly on interstate routes and for the movement of agricultural produce. He also disclosed that more than 30,000 additional vehicle conversion kits were expected to enter the Nigerian market from next week to expand conversion capacity ahead of the Christmas travel season. The post FG steps up CNG push with fuel station revival, staff vehicle conversion appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ‘We are on the ballot’ — Atiku vows to contest 2027 despite court ruling
item.description: Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has rejected the latest court ruling affecting the African Democratic Congress (ADC), insisting that he will remain in the race for the 2027 presidential election. Atiku, in a statement issued on Friday, said the judgment nullifying the David Mark-led leadership of the party and his presidential nomination should not be mistaken for the will of Nigerians. “Let no one mistake the latest court ruling for the will of the Nigerian people. No manipulation, conjecture or concoction can erase our place in this contest, silence our campaign or deny Nigerians the right to choose their future,” he said. “We are on the ballot, and the people must be allowed to decide.” The former vice-president accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of deploying political pressure, court manoeuvres and other tactics to weaken opposition parties ahead of the election. He alleged that those in power were attempting to compromise the voters’ register through “AI-generated photographs, false names and fictitious identities”. Atiku said such actions were aimed at making genuine political competition difficult and pushing Nigeria towards a one-party state. He also challenged the ruling party to defend its record before voters rather than rely on its political strength. “Those who boast of having thirty-two governors and claim to have bought, pressured or coerced leaders from other parties into their fold should have no reason to fear a free and fair contest,” he said. Atiku criticised the Tinubu administration over the removal of fuel subsidy, the depreciation of the naira, rising food prices and worsening insecurity, arguing that the government had failed to ease the hardship facing Nigerians. He said businesses had shut down, young people were leaving the country in search of opportunities, while banditry and kidnapping continued to threaten communities. “Look around you. Market stalls stand empty. Feeding your family has become a daily struggle. Fuel prices keep rising, and silent pain fills homes across the country,” he said. Atiku urged his supporters not to lose hope, insisting that he would not withdraw from the presidential contest despite the legal challenge. “Let me be clear to every Nigerian who has stood with us: I am in this race. I am not going anywhere. We will be on the ballot,” he said. “No threat, blackmail or court manoeuvre will make me abandon you or the cause we share.” He vowed that the opposition would resist attempts to turn Nigeria into a one-party state and called on the ruling party to face its opponents in a free, fair and credible election. “If those in power believe in their numbers and their record, let us meet at the polls in a free, fair and credible contest,” Atiku said. He added that his campaign would continue to focus on the cost of living and the need to make life more affordable for Nigerians. “Let me say this plainly: Bola cannot use the courts to escape the judgment of Nigerians at the ballot b

Atiku said such actions were aimed at making genuine political competition difficult and pushing Nigeria towards a one-party state. He also challenged the ruling party to defend its record before voters rather than rely on its political strength. “Those who boast of having thirty-two governors and claim to have bought, pressured or coerced leaders from other parties into their fold should have no reason to fear a free and fair contest,” he said. Atiku criticised the Tinubu administration over the removal of fuel subsidy, the depreciation of the naira, rising food prices and worsening insecurity, arguing that the government had failed to ease the hardship facing Nigerians. He said businesses had shut down, young people were leaving the country in search of opportunities, while banditry and kidnapping continued to threaten communities. “Look around you. Market stalls stand empty. Feeding your family has become a daily struggle. Fuel prices keep rising, and silent pain fills homes across the country,” he said. Atiku urged his supporters not to lose hope, insisting that he would not withdraw from the presidential contest despite the legal challenge. “Let me be clear to every Nigerian who has stood with us: I am in this race. I am not going anywhere. We will be on the ballot,” he said. “No threat, blackmail or court manoeuvre will make me abandon you or the cause we share.” He vowed that the opposition would resist attempts to turn Nigeria into a one-party state and called on the ruling party to face its opponents in a free, fair and credible election. “If those in power believe in their numbers and their record, let us meet at the polls in a free, fair and credible contest,” Atiku said. He added that his campaign would continue to focus on the cost of living and the need to make life more affordable for Nigerians. “Let me say this plainly: Bola cannot use the courts to escape the judgment of Nigerians at the ballot box.” The post ‘We are on the ballot’ — Atiku vows to contest 2027 despite court ruling appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: FinTribe Finance Fair 2026: Empowers Over 10,000 Women to Build Wealth and Financial Independence
item.description: Over 10,000 women gathered at the Landmark Event Centre, Victoria Island, Lagos, on October 31, 2026, for the fourth edition of FinTribe Finance Fair , a growing movement dedicated to helping African women move from financial awareness to wealth creation and ownership. Themed I CAN and powered by returning lead sponsor Sycamore, the event brought together financial experts, business leaders, entrepreneurs and influential personalities, including Funke Akindele , Omoni Oboli , BamBam , Sola Adesakin and Olufemi Shobanjo , for a day of practical financial education, inspiring conversations and meaningful opportunities. For FinTribe founder Jennifer Awirigwe , popularly known as Financial Jennifer, the fair represents a bigger mission: helping women gain the confidence and resources to take charge of their financial futures. “Financial education is important, but knowledge must eventually become action. We want women to leave Finance Fair knowing that they can save, invest, grow their income, build businesses and take ownership of their financial future,” she shared ahead of the event. Beyond Finance Fair, FinTribe is building a community where women learn about money and put that knowledge into practice . With a presence across 43 countries, the organisation has reached over 20,000 women through financial education, supported more than 5,000 women with capital market training and helped members collectively save and invest millions of dollars. Through its Wealth Builders Academy, savings and investment community, real estate initiatives and recently launched FinTribe App, the organisation continues to create opportunities for women to build healthier financial habits, develop investment confidence and work towards long-term financial independence. At the fair, award-winning filmmaker Omoni Oboli encouraged women to pursue their ambitions without neglecting their wellbeing, reminding them to take things one step at a time, prioritise rest and ask for help when needed. During the Financial Clinic, Sola Adesakin challenged women to become more intentional about their finances, emphasising the importance of earning, budgeting and turning income into real assets. She also introduced the four forces of money: Earnings, Expenses, Engines and Encumbrances. Olufemi Shobanjo of NGX Regulation Limited shared insights into capital market participation, while actress BamBam, marketing strategist and Woof Studios founder Adetutu Laditan, and Mercy Agbeti, popularly known as Christian Money Woman, contributed to conversations about building value, navigating opportunities and growing with purpose. Beyond Finance Fair, FinTribe is building a community where women learn about money and put that knowledge into practice . With a presence across 43 countries, the organisation has reached over 20,000 women through financial education, supported more than 5,000 women with capital market training and helped members collectively save and invest millions of dollars. Through its Wealth Builders Academy, savings and investment community, real estate initiatives and recently launched FinTribe App, the organisation continues to create opportunities for women to build healthier financial habits, develop investment confidence and work towards long-term financial independence. At the fair, award-winning filmmaker Omoni Oboli encouraged women to pursue their ambitions without neglecting their wellbeing, reminding them to take things one step at a time, prioritise rest and ask for help when needed. During the Financial Clinic, Sola Adesakin challenged women to become more intentional about their finances, emphasising the importance of earning, budgeting and turning income into real assets. She also introduced the four forces of money: Earnings, Expenses, Engines and Encumbrances. Olufemi Shobanjo of NGX Regulation Limited shared insights into capital market participation, while actress BamBam, marketing strategist and Woof Studios founder Adetutu Laditan, and Mercy Agbeti, popularly known as Christian Money Woman, contributed to conversations about building value, navigating opportunities and growing with purpose. One of the most memorable moments came during Funke Akindele’s session when a medical doctor and founder of Raffia Fashion Africa presented the actress with a pair of handcrafted raffia earrings . Funke immediately wore them, danced, invited the entrepreneur onto the stage, embraced her, prayed for her and publicly endorsed her business. The entrepreneur later shared on her instagram page that “she had saved to purchase a VIP ticket to the fair and had admired Funke for years”. What began as a simple audience interaction became a powerful demonstration of how visibility, encouragement and one meaningful connection can open doors for a growing business. Beyond the stage, women connected with financial institutions, explored investment opportunities and participated in financial education sessions. The fair also featured empowerment opportunities and giveaways, including children’s investment portfolios, stock units, a plot of land, a Zanzibar trip and getaway experiences supported by partner organisations. Sycamore returned as lead sponsor for the second consecutive year, alongside other partners supporting FinTribe’s mission to expand women’s access to financial knowledge and opportunities. item.title: Alaafin, number one ruler in Yorubaland – Oba Owoade
item.description: The Alaafin of Oyo, Oba Abimbola Akeem Owoade I, has declared that he is the number one traditional ruler in Yorubaland, citing the historical significance and contributions of the old Oyo Empire to Yoruba civilisation. The monarch made the assertion during an interview on Edmund Obilo’s channel, where he spoke on Yoruba unity, the historical position of the Alaafin and his plans for the development of Oyo. Asked whether the Alaafin was the supreme king in Yorubaland, Oba Owoade answered in the affirmative, maintaining that history supported the position. “Historically, yes. If you want to go by history and the contribution of Oyo to Yoruba civilisation, then I would say that the Alaafin is number one,” he said. He, however, dismissed suggestions that he was in competition with other prominent Yoruba monarchs, particularly the Ooni of Ife, over traditional supremacy. “I don’t fight for supremacy or whatever with anybody,” he said. On his commitment to the Yoruba race, the monarch said he regularly prayed for the progress of the people, stressing that the success of Oyo would bring honour to the entire Yoruba race. “I believe that when Oyo succeeds, the Yoruba in their entirety get honoured. That’s my belief,” he said. Speaking on the development of Oyo, Oba Owoade expressed optimism about ongoing infrastructure projects, particularly the proposed circular road and its planned dualisation. He said the project, which would connect areas including Infinity and Sabo, would improve the city’s appearance and contribute to its development. The Alaafin also discussed the forthcoming Oyo Empire Day, describing it as a three-day celebration expected to attract about 40,000 people. He explained that the event was designed to bring together communities and people historically connected to the old Oyo Empire, irrespective of their present locations. According to him, the celebration would provide an opportunity to reconnect with their roots, preserve Yoruba culture and deliberate on the future of coming generations. Explaining why the event was named Oyo Empire Day rather than Oyo Day, the monarch said the empire had a wider historical reach beyond the present-day Oyo community. “The Oyo Empire comprises a number of people and cities, not just one. That’s why we are trying to make sure that we come together, reconnect to our roots, preserve our culture, deliberate on how to move forward and make a better future for our children together,” he said. Oba Owoade further disclosed that a Hall of Fame would be established as part of the celebration to recognise individuals and communities that had made significant contributions to Yoruba civilisation, Oyo Empire history, culture and heritage. He added that attendance would not be restricted to people with ancestral links to Oyo, noting that anyone interested in Yoruba culture was welcome. “Everybody is invited. item.title: How High Tariffs, Cost Of Living Made Trump Unpopular In US Midterm Elections — Rep-Elect Adesanya
item.description: Member-elect of the Georgia House of Representatives (District 43) in the United States, Solomon Adesanya, has explained how the struggles facing American residents, including high tariffs and the cost of living, played a major role in the outcome of the 2026 midterm elections. “I will tell you that this election was about something much bigger than political parties. It was about the everyday struggle of ordinary people. It was about the mother working two jobs who still struggles to put food on the table,” Adesanya said while on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily on Friday. “It was about the father who works 40 hours a week but still cannot afford to get decent housing. And it was ultimately about the millions of Americans who are doing everything right, working hard, playing by the rules, and yet find themselves falling further behind.” ﻿ According to him, the message from voters was clear: that hard work should lead to economic security, not a lifetime of financial struggle. “People are tired of an economy where the cost of living keeps rising. American people and the people of the great state of Georgia want to know that their government sees them, hears them, and is prepared to act on their behalf. And that’s the message that I take from this election, and that’s the responsibility that I intend to carry into the next legislative session,” the lawmaker said. Adesanya also noted that affordability had been a crisis since President Donald Trump got into the Oval Office. “We first started with this tariff war, and what you would find is when the president increased the tariffs on Canada and Mexico — one of our strongest allies by way of NAFTA — we’re hurting Americans, and Georgians were suffering that the cost of living had shot up in an unbelievable fashion and, added to the war in Iran, that was a war that nobody wanted and that war ultimately made the president unpopular,” the legislator stated. “When I get out and, you know, speaking with people in my community and my constituents, it is remarkable how people thought that they supported President Trump to be president and somehow think their life is going to be better and they’re going to become richer. The opposite happened. Their lives are worse off. “Our agenda is for the everyday Americans, not the Elon Musks, not the wealthy.” Adesanya said Nigerian politicians must know that elections are not about them but the communities they serve. He also disclosed his plan to champion the legislation that raises the Georgia minimum wage to $15 per hour. “So affordability is really crushing people. item.title: 2027: Heaven won’t fall if Atiku isn’t on the ballot — Keyamo
item.description: Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, has said Nigeria would not suffer any catastrophe if former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar is excluded from the ballot for the 2027 presidential election. Keyamo made the remark in a post on X on Friday while reacting to the Federal High Court judgment that nullified Atiku’s nomination as the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC). The judgment, which also invalidated the David Mark-led executive of the party, has triggered reactions from political figures and opposition supporters. Keyamo questioned what he described as the inconsistent attitude of opposition parties towards the judiciary, arguing that political actors should respect court decisions regardless of whether they favour or hurt their interests. He recalled the Supreme Court’s 2019 judgment that invalidated the victories of All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates in Zamfara State, from the governorship to the state House of Assembly, and declared their Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) opponents winners. Atiku, who contested the 2019 presidential election on the PDP platform, had welcomed the ruling at the time, describing it as a victory for the rule of law. In a statement issued by his media adviser, Paul Ibe, the former vice-president said: “Nothing is as pleasing to the ears of believers, as justice being served in the holy month of Ramadan.” Keyamo also cited the Supreme Court’s February 13, 2020, judgment that nullified the election of David Lyon, the APC candidate for Bayelsa governor, a day before his scheduled inauguration. The ruling paved the way for PDP candidate Douye Diri to emerge as governor. The minister said the APC accepted the court’s decisions without attacking the judiciary, adding that opposition parties should not condemn judges when rulings go against them. On February 13, 2020, when the Supreme Court nullified the victory of the APC Governorship candidate in Bayelsa State, David Lyon, a day to his swearing in (when he was in fact inspecting the stadium to be used), the APC took it with equanimity on the chin. When the Supreme… pic.twitter.com/9SxlITLYX9 — Festus Keyamo, SAN, CON, FCIArb (UK) (@fkeyamo) November 6, 2026 “You cannot abuse judges and blackmail the judiciary when it doesn’t go your way,” he said. Keyamo further declared: “Heavens WILL NOT FALL IF A CERTAIN ATIKU ABUBAKAR IS NOT ON THE BALLOT IN 2027.” In Thursday’s judgment, Justice Peter Lifu ruled that the Mark-led caretaker committee was illegal and upheld the position of Nafiu Bala, a former ADC national deputy chairman from the North-East. The judge also invalidated decisions taken by the caretaker committee, including Atiku’s nomination as the party’s presidential candidate for the 2027 election. In an earlier reaction to the ruling, Keyamo said the judgment reinforced the principle that legal decisions should be based on facts and evidence rather than sentiments. item.title: Crowd fave Linux Mint update approaches, fresh from autumn release of Cinnamon desktop
item.description: Linux Mint 27 is expected next month, and it's starting to take shape. Its flagship desktop, Cinnamon 2.8, is already available. The team behind the popular, beginner-friendly Linux just released Cinnamon 2.8 , which will be the default desktop in Mint 27. Since 2014, Linux Mint versions have been based on the LTS releases of Ubuntu. Since a new LTS, Ubuntu 26.04 "Resolute Raccoon" arrived in late April , that means that a corresponding version of Mint is in development. The Mint project blog post last month revealed the codename: "Adrien." This is the first male codename since Mint 1.0 "Ada" in 2006, based on the first ever Ubuntu LTS release, 6.06 "Dapper Drake", but the project has run through the whole alphabet since then (except for the letter “Y”.) That blog also revealed it will have a new alarm clock app, but the subsequent Mint Blog post imparted more information. The Nemo file manager will gain a preview pane, there will be a new and much more capable system resource-monitor program called "Superlight", a new simple manager for compressed archive files (Zip and so on) called "Unfold," and a new, theme-able terminal emulator called "Velocitty." Mint also has a new Community Website , which uses GitHub to manage logins and eliminates the old website's dependency on PHP. Probably the most significant new feature, though, is that Mint 27 will restore system hibernation. Ubuntu supported hibernation in its early releases, but it has been disabled as standard since 12.04 "Precise Pangolin." Enabling it again is regularly discussed, for instance back in 2020 . As we discussed in some detail a year ago , it's a complicated subject and there's a lot that can go wrong. It seems that Mint's Clément Lefebvre feels he can sort this, and we hope it works out. Support is included in the new version of Cinnamon, among a host of other changes. Its Wayland support is no longer experimental, although the X11 session is still there so users won't be forced to use the new system. The Network Manager applet has better, simpler VPN support and Wi-Fi encryption handling. There are multiple improvements across the desktop: better handling of sound devices, keyboard input layouts, touchpads and gesture support, HiDPI display handling, and better search in the Settings app. The window list control has been upgraded, more things happen in the background for faster desktop starts, and it has better handling and storage of authentication and credentials, including the same Rust-based "oo7" secret store we mentioned in Fedora 45 . Screensaver handling is also mentioned – this is particularly problematic under Wayland, as XScreensaver maintainer Jamie Zawinski has covered with some feeling . The Mint blog mentioned this at the start of 2026 , when Lefebvre announced the new, slower, annual release schedule. The Mint project blog post last month revealed the codename: "Adrien." This is the first male codename since Mint 1.0 "Ada" in 2006, based on the first ever Ubuntu LTS release, 6.06 "Dapper Drake", but the project has run through the whole alphabet since then (except for the letter “Y”.) That blog also revealed it will have a new alarm clock app, but the subsequent Mint Blog post imparted more information. The Nemo file manager will gain a preview pane, there will be a new and much more capable system resource-monitor program called "Superlight", a new simple manager for compressed archive files (Zip and so on) called "Unfold," and a new, theme-able terminal emulator called "Velocitty." Mint also has a new Community Website , which uses GitHub to manage logins and eliminates the old website's dependency on PHP. Probably the most significant new feature, though, is that Mint 27 will restore system hibernation. Ubuntu supported hibernation in its early releases, but it has been disabled as standard since 12.04 "Precise Pangolin." Enabling it again is regularly discussed, for instance back in 2020 . As we discussed in some detail a year ago , it's a complicated subject and there's a lot that can go wrong. It seems that Mint's Clément Lefebvre feels he can sort this, and we hope it works out. Support is included in the new version of Cinnamon, among a host of other changes. Its Wayland support is no longer experimental, although the X11 session is still there so users won't be forced to use the new system. The Network Manager applet has better, simpler VPN support and Wi-Fi encryption handling. There are multiple improvements across the desktop: better handling of sound devices, keyboard input layouts, touchpads and gesture support, HiDPI display handling, and better search in the Settings app. The window list control has been upgraded, more things happen in the background for faster desktop starts, and it has better handling and storage of authentication and credentials, including the same Rust-based "oo7" secret store we mentioned in Fedora 45 . Screensaver handling is also mentioned – this is particularly problematic under Wayland, as XScreensaver maintainer Jamie Zawinski has covered with some feeling . The Mint blog mentioned this at the start of 2026 , when Lefebvre announced the new, slower, annual release schedule. LXQt 2.5 Cinnamon is not the only desktop environment that has moved to embrace Wayland while also maintaining its support for X.org. Almost exactly two years ago, we reported that the LXQt 2.1 included preliminary Wayland support . That project is very much still in active development, led by Jen-Lee "PCMan" Hong, and version 2.5.0 just appeared, almost simultaneously with Cinnamon 2.8. Before LXQt, "PCMan" developed the LXDE desktop – which is still around. There's an LXDE spin of Fedora 45, the Raspberry Pi OS uses some of its components, and last year when Debian 13 was released we also noted that its terminal emulator, LXTerminal, had just been updated. This release of LXQt removes its last dependency on an LXDE component – until now, it still used the old menu-cache . LXQt 2.5 is based on Qt 6.10, and it draws upon some of the components of KDE Plasma. One of these is libkscreen , which manages screens for Plasma. Version 6.8 of this drops X11 support – as does Plasma 6.8 itself – and that broke LXQt's Monitor Settings applet. The team are looking for a workaround and plan to fix this in a minor point release. Aside from this, the desktop's taskbar-style panel has improved sizing support, icon handling, and auto-hide, but most of the improvements in this release are in around its QTerminal terminal emulator. New LXQt versions usually appear twice a year, around April and November, so this version will likely be in Lubuntu 27.04 in about five months – and available in many other distributions, too. ®

item.title: Goalkeeper Jesus Owono considers quitting football after striker’s death – report
item.description: Equatorial Guinea goalkeeper Jesus Owono is reportedly considering retiring from football after his collision with Spanish striker Jesus de Miguel, who died following the incident. Owono was playing for Andorra FC when he collided with De Miguel while attempting to clear the ball during a match on Monday, November 2, 2026. The Tenerife forward was left on the pitch following the challenge and was taken to hospital, where he died the following morning from what was described as “accidental chest trauma”. Owono was sent off for the challenge and has reportedly been struggling emotionally following the striker’s death. According to Spanish publication Mundo Deportivo, the goalkeeper is considering walking away from professional football following the tragedy. Ana Maye, a close friend of Owono and general coordinator of the Equatorial Guinea men’s national team, said the incident had deeply affected him despite efforts to offer support. “No matter how much we tell him, he’s deeply saddened. “He’s very affected, especially for Jesús Miguel’s one-and-a-half-year-old son and for his widow. He doesn’t know how to handle all of this.” Jesus Owono, who has been receiving psychological support from his team, also released a statement expressing his grief following De Miguel’s death. In a social media post, he wrote: “These are the most difficult days of my life. I struggle to find the words, and I find it very hard to process what has happened. “I feel enormous pain at the loss of Jesus. I think of him, his family, and all the people who loved him. I know there will be many questions to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. “But right now, honestly, I cannot think about anything other than Jesus and the ⁠pain we are experiencing. Rest in ⁠peace, Jesus.” De Miguel’s funeral was held in his hometown of Navahermosa, in the province of Toledo, on Thursday, November 5. Hundreds of mourners, including family members and prominent figures in Spanish football, attended the burial to pay their final respects. Among those present were Real Madrid president Florentino Perez and Spain national team coach Luis de la Fuente. Meanwhile, Maye disclosed that Owono’s family had also been subjected to abuse following the incident, with some people reportedly targeting his relatives online and in person. She said: “They’re calling Jesús’s brother a murderer. He’s being heckled by his teammates, and even some parents are insulting him.” Vanguard News The post Goalkeeper Jesus Owono considers quitting football after striker’s death – report appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Supreme Court justices placed on US visa ban, retiring jurist reveals
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA — A retiring Justice of the Supreme Court, Justice Uwani Abba-Aji, disclosed on Friday that some justices of the court had been placed on a visa ban by the United States of America. Justice Abba-Aji, speaking during a valedictory session held to mark her retirement from the bench, said the travel ban followed a judgment of the apex court that she described as widely misinterpreted. She said: “My time on the Supreme Court bench was filled with challenges, some of which have served as additional opportunities to stand firm on the side of justice, regardless of the consequences. “One of such challenging judgments was widely misinterpreted and led to a travel ban to the United States of America being imposed on all members of the panel, a ban which still holds today.” Even though Justice Abba-Aji did not mention the specific case that led to the imposition of a US visa ban on Supreme Court Justices, Vanguard understands that it was connected to the legal tussle that followed the 2019 governorship election in Imo State. A seven-member panel of the Supreme Court, which included the current Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN), Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, and Justice Abba-Aji, had on January 14, 2020, nullified the election of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) candidate, Emeka Ihedioha, and ordered the swearing-in of the candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Senator Hope Uzodimma, who had initially finished fourth in the governorship election. In the lead judgment delivered by the CJN, the apex court ordered the immediate withdrawal of the Certificate of Return that had already been issued to Ihedioha by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). It ordered that a fresh Certificate of Return be issued to Uzodimma as the validly elected governor of Imo State. To arrive at the decision, the apex court panel vacated the concurrent verdicts of both the Court of Appeal and the Imo State Governorship Election Petitions Tribunal, which had earlier affirmed the PDP candidate as winner of the gubernatorial contest. The panel went ahead to add election results from 388 polling units, amounting to 213,295 votes, which were tendered before the tribunal by a police officer who testified as PW-54, but which INEC disowned. After all the votes were computed inside the courtroom, Uzodimma was declared the candidate who secured the majority of lawful votes cast at the election, a judgment that elicited wide reactions and protests. Other members of the panel, which was led by the then CJN, Justice Tanko Muhammad, were Justices Sylvester Ngwuta, Kayode Ariwola and Amiru Sanusi. Although Ihedioha subsequently approached the apex court again for a review of the judgment, which he insisted occasioned a miscarriage of justice, his application was refused. item.dc:creator: olufemiajasa
item.content:encoded: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA — A retiring Justice of the Supreme Court, Justice Uwani Abba-Aji, disclosed on Friday that some justices of the court had been placed on a visa ban by the United States of America. Justice Abba-Aji, speaking during a valedictory session held to mark her retirement from the bench, said the travel ban followed a judgment of the apex court that she described as widely misinterpreted. She said: “My time on the Supreme Court bench was filled with challenges, some of which have served as additional opportunities to stand firm on the side of justice, regardless of the consequences. “One of such challenging judgments was widely misinterpreted and led to a travel ban to the United States of America being imposed on all members of the panel, a ban which still holds today.” Even though Justice Abba-Aji did not mention the specific case that led to the imposition of a US visa ban on Supreme Court Justices, Vanguard understands that it was connected to the legal tussle that followed the 2019 governorship election in Imo State. A seven-member panel of the Supreme Court, which included the current Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN), Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, and Justice Abba-Aji, had on January 14, 2020, nullified the election of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) candidate, Emeka Ihedioha, and ordered the swearing-in of the candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Senator Hope Uzodimma, who had initially finished fourth in the governorship election. In the lead judgment delivered by the CJN, the apex court ordered the immediate withdrawal of the Certificate of Return that had already been issued to Ihedioha by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). It ordered that a fresh Certificate of Return be issued to Uzodimma as the validly elected governor of Imo State. To arrive at the decision, the apex court panel vacated the concurrent verdicts of both the Court of Appeal and the Imo State Governorship Election Petitions Tribunal, which had earlier affirmed the PDP candidate as winner of the gubernatorial contest. The panel went ahead to add election results from 388 polling units, amounting to 213,295 votes, which were tendered before the tribunal by a police officer who testified as PW-54, but which INEC disowned. After all the votes were computed inside the courtroom, Uzodimma was declared the candidate who secured the majority of lawful votes cast at the election, a judgment that elicited wide reactions and protests. Other members of the panel, which was led by the then CJN, Justice Tanko Muhammad, were Justices Sylvester Ngwuta, Kayode Ariwola and Amiru Sanusi. Although Ihedioha subsequently approached the apex court again for a review of the judgment, which he insisted occasioned a miscarriage of justice, his application was refused. Only one member of the panel, Justice Centus Nweze, gave a dissenting verdict that ordered Ihedioha’s reinstatement as governor, declaring the judgment that removed him from office a nullity. Justice Nweze then warned the Supreme Court panel about the consequences of the judgment, which he said was delivered in bad faith. “This decision of the Supreme Court will continue to haunt our electoral jurisprudence for a long time to come,” he warned. Meanwhile, at the valedictory session on Friday, Justice Abba-Aji who is exiting the apex court having reached the 70-year mandatory retirement age, said the US visa ban was part of the price she paid for her service on the bench. “Such inconveniences were a small price to pay to preserve the chastity of justice,” she added. In her address, the CJN, Justice Kekere-Ekun, extolled the virtues of the retiring jurist, who she said had served in various administrative capacities as a Clerical Assistant, Assistant Registrar, Acting Registrar and Higher Registrar since 1973, when she joined the judicial service in Borno State. She noted that Justice Abba-Aji had served at various Divisions of the Court in Benin, Abuja, Ekiti, Owerri and Kaduna since September 22, 2004, when she was elevated to the Court of Appeal, before she was promoted to the Supreme Court on January 8, 2019. “For many of us, particularly the women who have entered the Nigerian Judiciary in more recent years, Hon. Justice Abba-Aji’s career is part of the story of how the place of women in our Judiciary has evolved. “Long before the presence of women on the Bench became as familiar as it is today, she was already serving, quietly establishing a record of competence and service. “Hon. Justice Abba-Aji’s journey into the legal profession began at a time when the professional landscape was very different from what we know today. “Her leadership roles in the Federation of Muslim Women Associations of Nigeria and, particularly, her service as President of the National Association of Women Judges Nigeria (NAWJN), demonstrate that her interest in the progress of women was not merely incidental to her career. “She contributed to creating a space in which other women could find their voices and assume positions of leadership,” the CJN added. The post Supreme Court justices placed on US visa ban, retiring jurist reveals appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: The women who rode the blue wave
item.description: In this edition, we report on how the US midterms, which saw the Democrats make massive gains, also marked a series of historic firsts for women. Also the dark side to Bangkok's booming fertility industry, which attracts thousands of foreign patients seeking assistance from the Thai capital's state-of-the-art private clinics. Plus how an impoverished neighbourhood in El Salvador, once a no-go zone plagued by gang violence, is being transformed by women into a vibrant canvas for street art.

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang summoned by Congress over Chinese espionage concerns
item.description: Top Republican lawmakers have asked Jensen Huang to appear before Congress to answer questions after it was reported that US intelligence officials believe Nvidia’s chief executive has been targeted by a Chinese spying operation. The chairs of the House committees on China, foreign affairs, and intelligence wrote to Huang this week asking him to appear before a joint closed-door briefing for their committees on November 18. “Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the People’s Republic of China’s access to sensitive US technology and information,” representatives John Moolenaar, Brian Mast, and Rick Crawford wrote. Read full article Comments

item.title: Blue Origin unveils more thrust, less haste as New Glenn slips to 2027
item.description: New Glenn's return to flight has slipped to January 2027, according to the internal memo, viewed by The Register, from Blue Origin CEO Dave Limp, overshadowing the company's announcements of a new third stage and booster engine. Blue Origin has been rebuilding after its New Glenn rocket exploded during a ground test in May , extensively damaging the launchpad. A month later, the company's CEO, Dave Limp, said that Blue Origin "still plan[s] to fly again this year," which raised a few eyebrows in the space and rocket community. The detonation had pretty much destroyed the facility, and getting back into the launch business so quickly seemed optimistic. That timetable has now slipped. In the memo, Limp praised the team's efforts but said: "We're proactively updating our anticipated launch date to January 2027." A small slip given the damage, but one that leaves less breathing room before NASA's planned Artemis III demonstration mission, involving lunar technologies from Blue Origin and SpaceX, next year. The delay emerged as the Bezos-backed company unveiled GS3, a third stage for New Glenn , designed for missions including direct injection into geostationary orbit and Earth-escape trajectories. The company said: "GS3 is already under contract for a cislunar mission with a government customer scheduled to launch in 2028." Blue Origin says the stage is not required for its lunar lander architecture, although it could support sustained operations around the Moon. The company also unveiled Northstar , a booster engine it says has half the parts and 30 percent less mass than its BE-4, while increasing thrust from 640,000 to 715,000 pounds-force. The memo said the team had "found and fixed the issue that caused the anomaly," without elaborating. Limp said in August that the problem "originated at the main oxygen valve on one of the BE-4 engines" and that existing engines would need retrofitting, but did not explain how the valve failed or what changes were required. The memo added that the company would "continue sharing progress updates on Voyager ." ®

item.title: TikTok’s For You page needs to change, says the EU
item.description: The European Commission claims TikTok broke its online platform rules by offering a recommendation algorithm that creates a "rabbit hole effect" on users. In an announcement on Friday, the regulators allege TikTok's algorithm can harm users with "endless and repeated exposure" to content related to sadness, isolation, or body image. The findings come months after the EU Commission declared that TikTok's design is too "addictive." While TikTok has implemented controls to mitigate the algorithm's "rabbit hole effect," the Commission says its preliminary findings suggest that they're not effective. TikTok must now change the design of its For … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: No more Cybertrucks; Musk moves on from the angular metallic flop
item.description: Elon’s Edsel is no more. Last night Tesla CEO Elon Musk revealed on social media that his car company is calling time on its failed attempt to wrest control of the American pickup truck market. The Cybertruck will cease production in the middle of 2027, liberating that space in Tesla’s cavernous factory for other uses—more Cybercabs , most likely. Musk first revealed the Cybertruck in late 2019 , back when Tesla was still trading at a theoretically understandable price-to-earning ratio. The pickup's unusual angular shape owed more to low-res video game models than any concessions to practicality. At the time Musk made fanciful claims that the truck would use a stainless steel monocoque construction, telling his audience that “the body and bed don’t do anything useful” on a normal truck. While some race cars use carbon-fiber monocoques for strength and lightness, making a pickup truck with a stainless steel monocoque chassis would only make sense if someone had an awful lot of stainless steel lying around and needed something to do with it all. The truck was supposed to go on sale for less than $40,000, and Tesla made its usual stratospheric sales predictions that (had they been accurate) the bare metal EVs would be as ubiquitous as the Model 3 and Y. Read full article Comments

item.title: Tinubu arrives in Akwa Ibom to inaugurate projects, attend APC rally
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has arrived in Uyo, the Akwa Ibom State capital, for a working visit to inaugurate projects executed by Governor Umo Eno’s administration and participate in an All Progressives Congress rally. Tinubu arrived in the state on Friday as part of a two-state visit to Akwa Ibom and Rivers, marking his first major outing in the South-South since the APC began mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections. The President was welcomed at Victor Attah International Airport by Eno, government officials, APC leaders and a large crowd of supporters. During the visit, Tinubu is expected to inaugurate several projects at the airport, including its new international terminal building, the International Airport Hospital and the Ibom Aviation Village. He will also inaugurate the Airport-Okopedi Road, linking communities in Nsit Atai and Okobo Local Government Areas, and Ring Road 3, which connects Idoro Road to Ikot Ekpene Road through Uyo and Ibiono Ibom. Other projects scheduled for inauguration include the AKWA-GIS Office Complex, the Command and Control Centre and the ARISE Palm Resort. Following the project inaugurations, Tinubu is expected to attend an APC rally at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium in Uyo. The post Tinubu arrives in Akwa Ibom to inaugurate projects, attend APC rally appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 'Too early to draw conclusions' as bomb threat hoaxes target European countries
item.description: Several Irish media outlets reported receiving bomb threats on Friday as a wave of hoax alerts that had so far mainly targeted airlines continued across Europe, with more than a dozen new flights affected. No explosives have been found in any of the incidents so far. European authorities are scrambling to identify the sources of the threats, as FRANCE 24's Brussels correspondent Dave Keating reports.

item.title: Tinubu’s visit: Bus conveying women to welcome president involved in accident
item.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi Several people have sustained injuries on Wednesday after an Akwa Ibom State Transport Corporation (AKTC) bus conveying women to welcome President Bola Tinubu collided with a security vehicle along Oron Road, Uyo. The victims were reportedly among supporters mobilised to join Governor Umo Eno in welcoming the President, who arrived in Akwa Ibom State through Calabar for an official visit. The accident involved the bus, loaded with women heading towards the airport, and a security Hilux van with both vehicles were badly damaged in the collision, leaving several occupants injured and requiring emergency assistance. Nsikakabasi Akpan, who captured the aftermath of the accident, shared footage showing early responders and other persons struggling to evacuate injured victims from the wreckage of the vehicles. He described the incident as an accident along Oron Road involving a bus conveying women to the airport to receive the President and a security Hilux vehicle. Confirming the incident, Paul James, Public Relations Officer, Road Safety Operations, Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC), Akwa Ibom State Command, said the command had dispatched a response team to the scene. James, however, said the command was yet to establish the extent of casualties and the circumstances surrounding the collision. The reported accident cast a shadow over the build-up to Tinubu’s visit, which attracted supporters and political stakeholders who had gathered to receive the President and his wife, Senator Oluremi Tinubu. The presidential couple were subsequently received by Governor Eno at the Victor Attah International Airport, Uyo, marking the commencement of their engagements in the state. The President’s official visit featured the unveiling of the airport’s new terminal, a major aviation infrastructure project expected to facilitate the commencement of international flight operations from the Victor Attah International Airport. The circumstances surrounding the crash, including the feared death and number of injured victims, were yet to be officially established by the FRSC as of the time of filing this report. The post Tinubu’s visit: Bus conveying women to welcome president involved in accident appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Rocket Report: Artemis II literally tore through the atmosphere; New Glenn delay
item.description: Welcome to Edition 9.18 of the Rocket Report! Blue Origin packed a lot of news into one afternoon Thursday with the reveal of a new kick stage for the New Glenn rocket, a new rocket engine design, and the minor and widely expected delay for New Glenn's return-to-flight mission from December until January. The reconstruction of Blue Origin's wrecked launch pad at Cape Canaveral, Florida, continues apace after a catastrophic explosion nearly six months ago. There's a lot of pent-up demand from NASA, Amazon, and the Space Force for Blue Origin to get New Glenn back in action. As always, we welcome reader submissions , and if you don't want to miss an issue, please subscribe using the box below (the form will not appear on AMP-enabled versions of the site). Each report will include information on small-, medium-, and heavy-lift rockets as well as a quick look ahead at the next three launches on the calendar. SpaceX vets work on water-fed propulsion . Three brothers who worked at SpaceX in the Falcon 9 era are now building satellites that run on water, a potentially harvestable resource on the Moon and found all over the Solar System, Ars reports . In late 2022, the three Carlisle brothers founded Argo Space to build infrastructure in space. Their vision was not just in-space transportation but also removing the need to use propellants from Earth to move around the heavens. Argo Space's satellites will use water not only as a propellant, but also as a coolant and radiation shield. Read full article Comments

item.title: Northern lights could reach New York and Idaho this weekend as speedy solar wind races toward Earth
item.description: null The northern lights could put on an impressive display this weekend as a colossal coronal hole on the sun fires a stream of high-speed solar wind toward Earth. Minor (G1) geomagnetic storm conditions between Nov. 6 and Nov. 8, with a chance of moderate (G2) conditions on Nov. 7 and Nov. 8, according to NOAA's Space Weather Prediction Center (SWPC) . If G2 conditions materialize, the northern lights could be visible as far south as New York and Idaho. What is happening? The culprit behind the potential uptick in northern lights is a large coronal hole on the sun , a region where the sun's magnetic field opens up. They allow streams of charged particles known as the solar wind to escape more easily into space. Coronal holes appear darker in ultraviolet images because they are cooler and less dense than their surroundings. And this particularly large — and rather oddly shaped — coronal hole is sending some seriously speedy wind our way. The culprit is a large coronal hole in the sun, shaped a bit like a witch on a broom... (Image credit: NASA SDO) The U.K. Met Office forecasts solar wind speeds between 342 and 404 miles (550-650 kilometers) per second, considerably faster than the typical speed of around 249 miles (400 km) per second. The fast solar winds are expected to arrive around Nov. 6-7 and could persist through much of the weekend. It could interact with Earth's magnetic field , potentially triggering geomagnetic storms and fueling spectacular aurora shows. The stronger the storm, the farther south the northern lights can potentially be seen. A predictive model from NOAA's Space Weather Prediction Center showing speedy solar wind (radial velocity image lower left) arriving at Earth (green dot) around Nov. 6 and persisting through Nov. 9. (Image credit: NOAA's Space Weather Prediction Center) Where will auroras be visible? Under G1 conditions, auroras may be visible from northern Michigan and Maine, but if activity intensifies to G2 levels, skywatchers farther south, including those in New York and Idaho, could be in for a treat. But remember! Aurora forecasts are notoriously tricky. Much depends on the strength and orientation of the magnetic field carried by the incoming solar wind, particularly whether it points southward, allowing more energy to transfer to Earth's magnetic field. Northern Hemisphere aurora forecast courtesy of the U.K. Met Office To give yourself the best chance of seeing the northern lights, keep an eye on those aurora forecasts, head somewhere dark away from city lights if you can, with a view of the northern horizon. To stay updated on space weather and know the best times and places to catch auroras, consider using a space weather app tailored to your location. One app I recommend is "My Aurora Forecast & Alerts," available on both iOS and Android . Another great tool is the "Space Weather Live" app on iOS and Android , which offers more in-depth insights into current space weather conditions and their potential

item.title: Nine parties back ADC after David Mark’s leadership sack
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi Nine opposition parties under the Coalition for Democracy have rallied behind the African Democratic Congress ADC, describing Thursday’s Federal High Court judgment which dissolved the Senator David Mark-led leadership of the party and invalidate its presidential candidacy as “a dangerous escalation in what appears to be a systematic campaign to eliminate credible political opposition ahead of the 2027 general elections.” In a statement signed by Salihu Moh. Lukman, on behalf of the coalition parties, the group warned that what is happening to the ADC today can happen to every opposition party tomorrow. The Coalition for Democracy emerged from the G100 Opposition Summit held in Abuja on 31 August 2026. Its members are the ADC, Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Democratic Leadership Alliance (DLA), National Rescue Movement (NRM), Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Peoples Redemption Party (PRP), Social Democratic Party (SDP) and Youth Progressives Party (YPP). The platform describes itself as committed to defending Nigeria’s constitutional democracy, protecting political pluralism and ensuring free, fair, credible and competitive elections. The Coalition recalled that it had only a day earlier raised the alarm over Nigeria’s shrinking democratic space, citing attacks on opposition supporters, obstruction of political activities and “the increasing weaponisation of state institutions against political competitors.” “When opposition parties are attacked on the streets, frustrated by state institutions, and threatened with elimination through judicial pronouncements, Nigerians must ask whether the ruling party still intends to face any meaningful opposition at the ballot box,” the statement said. The Coalition said it respects the independence of the judiciary and the right of aggrieved parties to seek legal redress, but insisted that “the courts must never become instruments through which political competition is extinguished. “Those who seek to destroy the opposition in order to guarantee their own victory must understand that they are not merely threatening political parties; they are threatening the very foundations of the Republic. A government that cannot tolerate opposition has lost the moral authority to call itself democratic. “When a government becomes more afraid of the opposition than it is accountable to the people, democracy itself is in danger”, the parties added. It warned that the narrowing of democratic space “carries grave consequences for national stability,” adding: “No democracy can remain peaceful when citizens are denied meaningful political alternatives. “The ballot must remain the battlefield of democracy. No political party should be allowed to achieve through institutional manipulation what it fears it cannot achieve through the votes of Nigerians,” it said. The Coalition said it respects the independence of the judiciary and the right of aggrieved parties to seek legal redress, but insisted that “the courts must never become instruments through which political competition is extinguished. “Those who seek to destroy the opposition in order to guarantee their own victory must understand that they are not merely threatening political parties; they are threatening the very foundations of the Republic. A government that cannot tolerate opposition has lost the moral authority to call itself democratic. “When a government becomes more afraid of the opposition than it is accountable to the people, democracy itself is in danger”, the parties added. It warned that the narrowing of democratic space “carries grave consequences for national stability,” adding: “No democracy can remain peaceful when citizens are denied meaningful political alternatives. “The ballot must remain the battlefield of democracy. No political party should be allowed to achieve through institutional manipulation what it fears it cannot achieve through the votes of Nigerians,” it said. The Coalition declared its solidarity with the ADC in its decision to challenge the judgment through the appropriate judicial processes. It called on all opposition parties, civil society organisations, the Nigerian Bar Association, organised labour, the media and patriotic Nigerians “to unite in peaceful, lawful resistance against every attempt to undermine political pluralism. “Let it be known: the Coalition for Democracy will not stand by while Nigeria is reduced to a democracy without opposition, elections without alternatives, and ballots without genuine choices. An attack on one is an attack on all. We will resist it together”, the parties declared.
